records.description: At this Thai restaurant, customers can enjoy the wonderful scenery of Songjeong Beach under the rattan-decorated lighting. It offers a wide variety of Thai dishes, wines, and beverages.

records.name: Wootopia
records.description: At Wootopia, you can enjoy 2++ Grade Hanwoo chosen and grilled by the chef, with the view of Gwangalli Beach. From preparation to eating, the whole experience is one-of-a-kind. It’s a great place for a romantic night out.

records.name: Ubong (우봉)
records.menu: Aged Hanwoo sirloin, Hanwoo brisket shabu shabu hot pot
records.description: Ubong is a Hanwoo specialty restaurant with an open view of Dongbaek Island. From auction to slaughter to aging, the whole process is managed by experts to provide only the highest quality beef. The refined presentation of shabu shabu hot pot is also very popular.

records.name: Good Morning Hong Kong (굿모닝홍콩)
records.description: It is a cha chaan teng, a type of restaurant in Hong Kong best known for eating breakfast. You can enjoy meals and desserts here. The spice level is mild and accommodating to the Korean palate.

records.name: Burger in New York (버거인뉴욕)
records.menu: Single Patty New York Burger, Special Burger
records.description: Every day, this shop makes patties with carefully selected Grade 1 Hanwoo and buttery brioche buns to provide burgers true to New York flavors. The exterior and interior decor also takes you to a street in New York.

records.name: Banpin (반핀)
records.menu: Char siu rice bowl, Mapo tofu
records.description: Serving casual dishes inspired by Taiwanese food, this restaurant is very popular among the young generation. The customer’s favorites are rice bowls with toppings grilled over binchotan. They also have light side dishes that go well with meals or beer.

records.name: Bokseong Banjeom (복성반점)
records.description:
Bokseong Banjeom is a Chinese restaurant that has been operating for two generations for more 
than 50 years. Since appearing in famous TV shows, it has been garnering even more crowd.
The signature dish is Jjamppong, topped with generous portions of seafood and onions.

records.name: Chef Lee (쉐프리)
records.menu:
French Rack Lamb(under 5 months, 200g) ￦72,000
Osso Buco ￦65,000
records.description: This Italian restaurant, run by an owner-chef with an acclaimed career, presents delicious dishes that also pair well with wine. While fancy decorations seem to be popular these days, when it comes down to food, it has to taste good.

records.name: Busan (부우사안)
records.menu: Beijing duck (same-day reservation), Lunch Set B
records.description: This authentic Chinese restaurant, famous for its Beijing Duck, is highly recommended for special occasions. It’s fun to see the whole Beijing duck before they are carved and served.

records.name: Stone Street
records.description: Wood-fired casual pizza and pasta are popular stars at this restaurant. The ricotta cheese used in cooking is freshly made every day. Its signature dish is the green grape salad with naan, strongly recommended by the regulars.

records.name: Sandong Wantang Gyojagwan
records.description: Operated by a Chinese owner, it feels as though a restaurant in China was relocated to Korea. It specializes in dumplings and offers unfamiliar and authentic mainland Chinese flavors that are not localized.

records.name: Samhyeongje Ori (삼형제오리)
records.menu: Lamb skewers for two, Duck barbecue
records.description: This is the only Korean branch of the Beijing duck franchise based in China. The signature dish is charcoal-grilled duck barbeque, but lamb skewers made of lamb ribs are also popular. Reservation is a must for the grilled duck.

records.name: Seokgisidae Main Branch (석기시대 본점)
records.description: Opened in 1987, this restaurant specializes in Chinese dumplings. It is known for affordable and tasty dumplings and five-spice steamed pork. It is frequented by local regulars for casual dining and drinks.

records.name: Osteria Aboo (오스테리아 어부)
records.menu:
Signature Tasting Course(1 person) ￦148,000
La carbonara ￦33,000
records.description: Instead of catering to the Korean palate, this restaurant presents the flavors of Italy as closely as possible for those who love authentic taste. While it is located in Busan, the restaurant’s food will take you to Italy.

records.name: Can Wei (칸웨이)
records.menu: Course meal for 1, Sweet and Sour Pork
records.description: It is a high-end Chinese restaurant presented by an owner who has organized various international events as the manager of Chinese and Korean restaurants at Lotte Hotel. With plenty of accommodations for children, the venue is great for family dining. The restaurant’s signature is the Chinese course meal.

records.name: Go-ok (고옥)
records.description: It is a famous restaurant in Busan known for making hitsumabushi popular. They use coal to grill eels and close early when the prepared ingredients are sold out. It is first come, first served without reservations.

records.name: Glass and Bottle (글라스 앤 보틀)
records.menu: Perilla oil and myungnan cappellini, Negitoro tartare
records.description: Glass and Bottle is a small wine bar owned by a married couple that resembles small Japanese bistros inside alleyways. Its Japanese-style casual cuisine goes very well with wine. Reservation is a must as there are very few tables.

records.name: Angtan (앙탄)
records.description: Located on the banks of the Nakdong River, this quiet and laid-back restaurant offers stunning views and a menu of duck courses. After the delightful course, dried persimmon rolls, their signature dessert, conclude the wonderful meal.

records.name: Kyoto Donburi Main Branch (교토돈부리본점)
records.description: The donburi specialty restaurant is popular for tonkatsu donburi made from Jeju black pig and salmon belly donburi. The quality of food is very high. The ingredients and the sauces used are all made from scratch.

records.name: Nagahama Mangetsu (나가하마 만게츠)
records.menu:
Nagahama Ramen ￦11,000
Nagahama Ramen Gyoza Set ￦18,000
records.description: It is a famous Japanese ramen restaurant in Haeridan-gil and is the only Korean branch of Fukuoka’s famous ramen restaurant. In recent years, it has become a mandatory stop for young people who visit the Haeundae area. The waiting begins at the time of its opening.

records.name: Noneun Bada (노는바다)
records.description: This Japanese izakaya restaurant is famous for konowata, which are salted guts of a sea cucumber. People come here from afar to experience their konowata. Because of the long wait, customers’ stay is limited to two hours.

records.name: Tokyo Table Main Branch (동경밥상 본점)
records.description: The owner-chef, who trained for a long time at Jyubako, a 240-year-old eel specialty restaurant in Japan, presents the authentic Jyubako-style grilled eel. The exterior and interior decor will also make you feel like you are in Japan.

records.name: Shun (슌)
records.description: This is a conveyor belt sushi bar with sushi freshly made by an experienced chef of over 25 years. They use rice produced in Jwacheon, and every item is the same price. The chef also makes and serves new pieces upon request.

records.name: Sushi Mireune (스시미르네)
records.description:
Sushi Mireune is one of the restaurants that led the popularization of sushi in Korea. It has also won the Korea Popular Brand Award for its management integrity. 
The restaurant is especially known for signature items such as mulhoe.

records.name: Sushi Sim Takai (스시심 타카이)
records.description: Susi Sim Takai opens two reservation slots each for lunch and dinner. The omakase course prepared by experienced chefs is satisfying in both taste and affordability. The fact that it takes 3 months to book a seat proves the restaurant’s massive popularity.

records.name: Yasumaru (야스마루)
records.description: The restaurant started out to present good food when people lose their appetite in the summer. But it’s known for the long queue regardless of the season. It’s known for parang guksu noodles with a unique appearance and not having a signboard.

records.name: Jungang Momil (중앙모밀)
records.description: Opened in 1956, this restaurant has been specializing in udon and buckwheat noodles for over 60 years. Busan’s older generations have childhood memories of coming here with their parents on special days. Here, it’s easy to spot three generations of families dining together.

records.name: King Kong Sushi (킹콩스시)
records.description: The sushi restaurant is known for its high value for the price. It serves fresh assorted sushi at a reasonable price. Many customers also order takeout or delivery here.

records.name: Taiga Tempura (타이가 텐푸라)
records.description: This is one of the restaurants that led the popularity of tendon (tempura rice bowl) in Busan. The high-quality tendon uses the recipe taught by Fukuoka’s famous tendon specialty store, Tempura Takao. Cooking begins at the time of ordering.

records.name: Tonshou (톤쇼우)
records.menu:
Berkshire K Special Roast Katsu ￦18,500
Hirekatsu ￦12,500
records.description: This is the main branch of the famous tonkatsu specialty store Tonshou. The restaurant selects quality ingredients and makes amazing tonkatsu through four stages: low-temperature frying, high-temperature frying, resting, and charcoal grilling.

records.name: Samseong Milmyeon (삼성밀면)
records.description: This milmyeon specialty restaurant has maintained its original taste for 60 years. It is also the only remaining milmyeon restaurant run by the first-generation owner. What more is there to say?

records.name: Busan Yakkong Milmyeon Igidae Main Branch (부산약콩밀면 이기대본점)
records.description: To make milmyeon more flavorful and healthy, they applied 40 years of know-how to create a unique recipe using natural brine from yakkong soybeans, hamcho (glasswort), and tot (hijiki) and vinegar made of kelp produced in Gijang.

records.name: Myeonchaeum (면채움)
records.description: To make milmyeon healthier, this restaurant uses five different grains to make its own noodles. The broth is boiled for 48 hours, and the sauce incorporates fruits and vegetables for natural flavor. Bibim mandu, a nostalgic dish for the locals, is also popular here.

records.name: Daeyeon Milmyeon (대연밀면)
records.menu: Bibim milmyeon, Deulkkae kalguksu (hand-cut noodle soup with perilla seeds)
records.description: Established in 2011, this milmyeon restaurant has been popular among the locals ever since.It serves the authentic milmyeon that’s true to the basics. The queue is also quite long, but it’s well worth the wait.

records.name: Hapcheon Gukbapjip (합천국밥집)
records.menu:
Dwaejigukbap(pork soup with rice) ￦12,000
Steamed pork ￦40,000 / 45,000
records.description: This restaurant is indispensable when discussing dwaejigukbap in Busan. It’s differentiated from other gukbap joints by the clear and lean broth. Large chunks of domestic pork are generously served in the soup.

records.name: Jeongjitgan (정짓간)
records.description: This place, named after the Gyeongsangdo dialect for “kitchen,” cooks dwaejigukbap by boiling the broth for 48 hours in a cauldron. The steamed pork can be either pork belly or jowl meat, and the toppings, temperature, and level of spice for the soup can also be selected.

records.name: Uri Dwaejigukbap (우리돼지국밥)
records.menu: Dwaejigukbap (pork soup with rice), Assorted steamed pork
records.description: Since 1975, it has been operating for three generations. It boils the broth for 24 hours and serves the soup with the traditional toryeom method. It uses the whole pig and immediately serves customers their favorite parts upon request.

records.name: Subok Dwaejigukbap (수복돼지국밥)
records.menu: Suyuk Baekban (Steamed pork with set meal), Dwaejigukbap (pork soup with rice)
records.description: The restaurant serves domestic pork meat and innards, and sundae, kimchi, and kkakdugi made from scratch. From the early hours, they pay special care to the preparation of food and provide clean dining rooms and plenty of parking spaces.

records.name: Bugwang Dwaejigukbap (부광돼지국밥)
records.menu:
Dwaejigukbap(pork soup with rice) ￦10,000
Steamed pork ￦30,000 / 35,000
records.description: This authentic dwaejigukbap restaurant has been in business for more than 40 years for three generations. Kimchi and kkakdugi are made from scratch, and their insistence on fresh quality ingredients shows why they have been popular for so long.

records.name: Suhyang Bapsang (수향밥상)
records.description:
This loach specialty restaurant is beloved by families. 
The rich loach soup is the most popular dish. They make a lot of effort to use healthy and quality ingredients, such as directly operating a fish farm.

records.name: Haemul Wangchang Kalguksu (해물왕창칼국수)
records.menu:
Haemul Wangchang Kalguksu
(hand-cut noodles with seafood for two) ￦12,000
Mul milmyeon with yukjeon ￦8,000
records.description: Clams for the broth are supplied every day from Goheung, Jeolla Province. The dough for the kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) that goes into the seafood soup is made freshly and rested each morning. The noodle soup, made with fresh ingredients and tender loving care, is never going to be unpopular.

records.name: Halmae Jaecheopguk (할매재첩국)
records.menu: Jaecheop set meal, Jaecheop with rice
records.description: The owner started selling jaecheopguk (freshwater clam soup) in Gupo in 1950 and moved to today’s location 20 years ago. Since it opens early, many customers come here to eat breakfast. It also has a directly managed branch in Seoul.

records.name: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon (동래할매파전)
records.menu:
Dongnae halmae pajeon ￦28,000 / 40,000
Dongnae steam conch ￦30,000
records.description: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon is a famous restaurant that has been in business for four generations. It continues the tradition of Dongnae pajeon, Busan’s signature local food. The green onion pancakes, with more presence in the material than in the photos, will keep exceeding your expectations with each bite.

records.name: Park Hae-yun Tongyeong Bapsang (박해윤 통영 해물밥상)
records.description: This hanjeongsik restaurant uses fresh seafood supplied from Tongyeong. It is also beloved as the venue for special occasions such as first birthdays and family meetings for marriage, with quality food, a spacious parking lot, and a pleasant interior.

records.name: Wonjo Kkorigomjip (원조꼬리곰집)
records.menu:
Steamed Hanwoo tail Slices ￦92,000
Oxtail soup ￦27,000
records.description: Opened in 1980, it is a longtime local favorite. The skin is preserved using a special method for a softer texture. The secret is to boil a large amount of meat for a long time, which is staying true to the basics.

records.name: Hadong Jaecheopguk (하동재첩국)
records.description: This is an especially popular freshwater clam soup restaurant in the area populated by similar restaurants. They only use domestic freshwater clams from Seomjingang River and boil them after washing several times after soaking it in saltwater. Freshwater clam soup is said to help liver and stomach health. The restaurant also researched how to serve freshwater clam as raw fish and steamed, and helped establish.

records.name: Ha Gi-yeon Jinju Naengmyeon (하기연진주냉면)
records.description: Jinju naengmyeon is made of seafood broth with anchovies, clams, and kelp and garnished with yukjeon (meat pancakes). It’s a rare delicacy, and only a few masters have been professionally trained to make it. This restaurant is characterized by using only black buckwheat from Jeju Island to make noodles.

records.name: Janganjip (장안집)
records.description: Next to this Hanok-style restaurant is a mountain stream, and nearby is a famous temple called Jangansa. The large parking lot and private rooms are great for families and groups. It is also famous for duck soup.

records.name: Lee Family’s Kalguksu (이가네 칼국수)
records.description: Sasang Intercity Bus Terminal is famous for the good restaurants in its area, including this one. Whether it’s seafood kalguksu, dumplings made 100% from scratch, or milmyeon, any choice will guarantee your satisfaction.

records.name: Lee Family’s Tteokbokki (이가네 떡볶이)
records.menu: 1 serving of tteokbokki, 1 serving of tteokboki and twigim
records.description: Lee Family’s Ttokbokki is well-known throughout Korea by appearing on famous TV shows. It’s a must-visit stop for touring the original Busan city center, always filled with bustling customers.

records.name: Useong Samgyetang (우성삼계탕)
records.description: Useong Samgyetang is a samgyetang specialty store that has only made samgyetang for more than 40 years. It is known for its thick, garlic-flavored broth. This longtime specialty restaurant is always bustling with local regulars, and the customers love the fried gizzards offered for free.

records.name: Mongtteul (몽뜰)
records.description:
It is a restaurant specializing in Hanwoo barbecue, but just as many customers also come here for yukhoe bibimbap and chadol doenjang jjigae.
The yukhoe bibimbap sauce is not just gochujang but is made with an original secret recipe, and chadol doenjang jjigae is also famous for its taste.

records.name: Cho Gwangsim Minsok Wangsundae (조광심민속왕순대)
records.description: Pisundae, made of pork blood curds and entrails, are made and served freshly because they cannot be frozen. All menu items use domestic ingredients. The restaurant doesn’t open for business on Mondays but opens a free kitchen for the underprivileged. The kindness of the owners always attracts local regulars.

records.name: Halamejip Hoeguksu (할매집회국수)
records.description: It is a famous restaurant that has been operating for more than 70 years and is one of the leading restaurants in Busan’s original city center. Hoeguksu is the signature item with its unique spicy taste and stingray topping. Many customers return steadily because they can’t forget the taste of the food here.

records.name: Natan Yakseonyori (나탄약선요리)
records.description: Inspired by traditional Korean cuisine, this restaurant excludes all chemical seasonings and preserves the original taste of the ingredients. It also adds medicinal herbs for therapeutic effects. The service is considerate and caring throughout the meal.

records.name: Budamyeonok (부다면옥)
records.menu:
Pure buckwheat naengmyeon ￦12,000
Steamed Hanwoo sampler ￦20,000
records.description: For a clean and refreshing taste, this Pyongyang naengmyeon specialty restaurant uses the shank from Hanwoo beef and various vegetables to make the broth. Each of the ingredients is boiled in different pots and cooled in the traditional way. The depth of their flavors is indescribable through photos.

records.name: Bon Gogalbi (본 고갈비)
records.description:
Oven-grilled mackerel at 500 degrees is the most popular dish at this restaurant. 
The mackerel is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside.
It is particularly popular for the numerous side dishes that can be refilled for free at the self-bar.

records.name: 88 Dwaejigalbi (88돼지갈비)
records.description:
The taste of the masterfully grilled meat is indescribably good.
This 40-year-old restaurant with a rustic and quaint entrance is a local favorite that specializes in marinaded barbecue.

records.name: Dolsotbapjip (돌솥밥집)
records.menu: Sundubu jjigae and stone pot bibimbap,  Doenjang jjigae and stone pot bibimbap
records.description:
Here, you can make bibimbap by mixing namul with rice served in a hot stone pot and eat it with doenjang jjigae or sundubu jjigae that are accompanied.
Operated for 40 years, the experience at this restaurant speaks for itself.

records.name: Maengyeosa Yukjeon Yukhoe (맹여사육전육회)
records.description:
Yukjeon and yukhoe, already tasty on their own, can be enjoyed in various ways here.
Thanks to the meticulous service, yukjeon is cooked a little bit at a time for the perfect warmth at the time of eating. No wonder this place is beloved by many.

records.name: Eunha galbi
records.menu: yangnyeom galbi (grilled marinated galbi), dwaeji moksal (grilled pork shoulder), saeng galbi (grilled galbi), samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), doenjang jjigae (soybean paste jjigae)
records.description: At this restaurant, you can have dwaeji-galbi (porkshort ribs), moksal (pork neck), and samgyeopsal(pork belly). It is neither big nor fancy; however, the side dishes and meat are delicious, so it's always full of customers. The pork ribs marinated in homemade seasoning are the most popular dish on the menu.

records.name: Hapcheon gukbapjip
records.menu: ttaro gukbap (rice and soup), suyuk baekban (boiled pork slices set menu), suyuk (boiled pork slices), modum suyuk (assorted boiled pork slices), sundae (Korean sausage)
records.description: This restaurant serves dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice) that has a clear broth. When you order dwaeji-gukbap, the broth is poured over pork innards, such as intestines and uterus, several times before serving. Different variations of gukbap are available, all with rice on the side: modeum ddaro (with assorted meat (pork, sundae, and pork intestines)); sundae ddaro (with Korean sausage); naejang ddaro (with pork intestines); or ddaro (with only pork). It is best enjoyed with plenty of chives as is the custom in Busan.

records.name: Gijangson kalguksu
records.menu: son kalguksu (handmade noodle soup), bibim sonkalguksu(spicy handmade noodles), naeng kalguksu (cold handmade noodle soup), gimbap
records.description: This restaurant specializes in Gyeongsang-do style kalguksu (handmade noodle soup), served in anchovy broth and topped with crown daisy and Chinese chives. It is light and refreshing, with a hint of sesame seeds and minced garlic. The noodles are made by rolling out the dough, and the only side dish is kkakdugi (radish kimchi). The dish is simple, but generously portioned, with a homemade taste.

records.name: Ssangdungi dwaejigukbap
records.menu: dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), naejang gukbap (offal and rice soup), suyuk baekban (boiled pork slices set menu), dwaeji suyuk (boiled pork slices), naejang suyuk (boiled offal slices)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in dwaeji-gukbap(pork soup with rice) and is so popular that there is often a line out the door. Rice is placed in an earthenware pot, and then the soup is poured over it and removed multiple times before serving. The soup is best enjoyed by adding plenty of jeongguji(seasoned Chinese chives). The suyuk (boiled pork) made with hanjoengsal (pork jowl) is also recommended.

records.name: Samo bulgogi
records.description: This meat restaurant offers two dishes: thinly sliced pork belly and seasoned pork ribs. It also serves a variety of side dishes that go well with the meat, as well as sikhye (sweet rice punch) for dessert. The seasoned crab is a popular side dish. This is a place where you can enjoy a meal at an affordable price.

records.name: Eonyang bulgogi busanjip
records.menu: Eonyang bulgogi, deungsim (grilled sirloin), saeng galbitsal (grilled boneless galbi), yuk sashimi (sliced raw beef)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in Eonyang-style bulgogi, which is made with thinly sliced highquality beef that is marinated in a unique Eonyang seasoning and then grilled over charcoal. The taste is exquisite, and it is best enjoyed wrapped in the white kimchi that is served with it.

records.name: Eunhae galchi
records.menu: galchi gui (braised cutlassfish), galchi jjigae (cutlassfishjjigae), galchi jorim(braised cutlassfish)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in fresh Jeju kalchi(hairtail) dishes. When you order extra-large grilled kalchi, the pieces are thick and the size of your hand, and have an exquisite texture that is firm and tender. The kalchi-jjigae (hairtail stew) with a doenjang (soybean paste) base has a light and refreshingly spicy taste and is also popular. The side dishes, along with three kinds of salted fish, that they serve are also delicious and neat.

records.name: Dongbaekseom hoetjip
records.menu: jeomsim teukseon hoe jeongsik (lunch special sliced raw fish set), hoe course (sliced raw fish full-course set menu), sekkosi (bone-in sliced raw fish)
records.description: This wild-caught sashimi restaurant is a local favorite because their fish is so fresh. When you order sashimi, you are also served a variety of seafood and tempura. In Busan, it is customary to dip sashimi in ssamjang (soybean paste), and you can make sushi by placing sashimi on sushi rice. They serve maeuntang (spicy fish soup) and steamed fish as part of your meal.

records.name: Saechong hoetjip
records.menu: jayeonsan hoe (sliced raw wild fish), isigari(roughscale sole)
records.description: Here, you can enjoy ishigari (roughscale sole) sashimi, which is known for its savory, fatty flavor. Other wild-caught fish are also available, so you can enjoy sashimi of various high-quality fish such as domi (sea bream) and gajami (sole). Enjoy the rich-flavored maeuntang (spicy fish soup), which is served afterward.

records.name: Chopilsal dwaejigui
records.menu: kkeopdegi (pork rinds), sogeum gui (salt-grilledmeat), dwaeji galbi (grilled pork galbi), dwitgogi (various pork cuts), daepae samgyeopsal (grilled thin-sliced pork belly), tongsamgyeop kimchi jjigae (pork and kimchi jjigae)
records.description: This is a popular grilled pork restaurant in Haeundae. Its flavorful, chewy meat pairs well with the green onions and sauce. The signature dish is the honeycomb-cut pork rinds. They offer a very satisfying meal for the price.

records.name: Geodae sutbulgui
records.menu: hanu yangnyeom galbi (grilled marinated Korean galbi), ansim (grilled tenderloin), galbitsal (grilled boneless galbi), deungsim (grilled sirloin), anchangsal (grilled thin skirt), Pyeongyang naengmyeon (pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles), gomtang (beef bone soup), jeomsim teukseon (lunch special)
records.description: This restaurant offers high-quality 1++ grade Korean beef in a luxurious setting. Their specialty is yangnyeom-galbi (marinated short ribs), but they also serve a variety of other cuts, such as short ribs, eye filet, and outside skirt. The regular side dishes are usually tasty, and the Pyongyang naengmyeon is great for refreshing your palate.

records.name: Budamyeonok
records.menu: soonmemil naengmyeons (cold buckwheat noodles), sari (side order), matbogi hanu suyuk (Korean beef suyuk taster), hanu hanmari kkorisuyuk (boiled Korean oxtail slices), kkori gomtang (oxtail and beef bone soup), yukgaejang (spicy beef soup)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in Pyongyang-style naengmyeon, which are noodles served in a chilled, clean-tasting broth. They normally offer only two dishes: Pyongyang naengmyeon and suyuk (steamed pork), but in winter, they also serve gomtang (ox bone soup) and yukgaejang (spicy beef stew).

records.name: Ajeossi daegutang
records.menu: daegutang (codfish soup), daegu ppoljjim (braised codfish head)
records.description: Here, the popular dish is daegu-tang, a cod soup with a refreshing broth. It is characterized by the addition of cod heads to give the soup flavor. The side dishes, which include various jangajji (pickled side dishes) and mungae-jeot (salted sea squirts), are delicious. The restaurant is also a favorite of artist Heo Young-man and celebrity Jeong Woo.

records.name: Yeongnam dwaeji
records.menu: samgyeop loseu (grilled pork belly), samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), moksal (grilled pork shoulder), yangnyeom samgyeomn loseu (grilled marinated pork belly), hangjeongsal (grilled pork neck), mul naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles), bibim naengmyeon (spicy buckwheat noodles), chadol doenjang (beef brisket soybean paste jjigae)
records.hours:
1st floor: 11:30 a.m. a.m. - 10:30 p.m. (Last seating: 9:30,Last order: 10:00 a.m.)
2nd floor: 11:30 a.m. a.m. - 9:30 p.m.(Last seating: 9:30, Last order: 10:00 a.m.)
records.description: This restaurant offers a variety of high-quality grilled beef and pork. The meat is grilled to perfection for you, so you can enjoy your meal without any hassle. Seasoned green onions and mel-jeot (salted anchovies) are also served with the meat, and make for a delicious combination. A popular dish is mul-naengmyeon, noodles in a chilled, savory broth with a meaty flavor.

records.name: Mujinjang hoetjip
records.menu: bungjangeo hoe (sliced raw conger eel), modum hoe (assorted sliced raw fish), dodari (ridged-eye flounder), chamgajami (flouder), dom (sea bream), maeuntang (spicy fish stew)
records.description: This is a long-standing restaurant that serves anago (conger eel). Try the dried anago sashimi, which is best enjoyed dipped in makjang (fermented soybean-and-barley sauce). The spicy maeuntang (spicy fish soup) that comes with the anago sashimi is also tasty. The restaurant is located in a scenic spot overlooking the sea and offers stunning views.

records.name: Tambok
records.menu: ttalgi mille-feuille (strawberry mille-feuille), tarte chocolat, orange cocoa madeleine, muhwagwa keurimchijeu financier (fig butter cream cheese financier), Haenam bamgoguma crème brulée (sweet potato crème brulée), Americano, caffe latte
records.description: This abalone restaurant offers a luxurious dining experience. The basic set includes abalone rice, abalone porridge, and grilled abalone. You can choose between miyeok (seaweed), hijiki seaweed, and gondre (Korean thistle) as a garnish for the abalone rice and mix in some gewoo sauce (a sauce made with abalone innards) and abalone paste.

records.name: Mimiru
records.menu: jjajangmyeon (noodles in black bean sauce), jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup), junghwa deopbap (chinese bibimbap), sacheon laziji (Sichuan spicy stir-fried chicken), yuringi (deep-fried chicken in hot and sour soy sauce), gungbogijeong (kung pao chicken), menbosha (fried shrimp sandwich), tangsuyuk (deep-fried pork with sweet and sour sauce)
records.description: This Chinese restaurant is a popular spot in Busan. You can enjoy great Chinese food at a reasonable price. One outstanding item on the menu is the Sichuan laziji (mala chicken), which features a harmonious blend of spicy flavors and ingredients. All dishes come topped with a fried egg.

records.name: BUSAN
records.menu: sacheonsik baechujjim (Sichuan braised napa cabbage), chashu, maui sangsu (spicy fried cellophane noodles and ground pork), sannibaegyuk (garlic pork on a bed of thin-sliced cucumber), dim sum, Peking duck, lunch set, dinner set
records.description: This modern Chinese restaurant is decorated black tones. The signature dish is Peking duck with crispy skin, made properly in a dedicated wood-fired oven. They also serve a variety of familiar Chinese dishes with a modern twist. Two unique dishes that are noteworthy are their ma-yi-shang-shu (spicy fried cellophane noodles and ground pork) and suan-nibai-rou (pork with spicy garlic sauce).

records.name: Sandong Wantang gyojagwan
records.menu: wonton soup, gogi mandu (meat mandu), kimchi mandu, mul mandu (boiled mandu), samsaek modum mandu (tricolor mandu), gajiyori (eggplant), tomato gyeran bokkeum (stir-fried tomato and egg), ohyang jangyuk (five-spice pork), mapa dubu (spicy bean curd)
records.description: This is a place where you can enjoy wontons and dumplings at a reasonable price, and you can experience the flavors of mainland China. The dishes and anju (side dishes for drinking) arereasonably priced, making it an excellent place for a drink. The mapo tofu (tofu and minced meat in a spicy sauce) and eggplant dishes are highly recommended.

records.name: Donggyeong bapsang
records.menu: donggyeongsik minmul jangeo deopbap (Tokyo-style stirfried eel with rice (unaju)) , nagoyasik minmul jangeo deopbap (Nagoya style stir-fried eel with rice (hitsumabushi)), minmul jangeo deopbap (stir-fried eel with rice)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in rice topped with grilled eel, which are available in Tokyo-style unaju and Nagoya-style hitsumabushi. After eating some of the rice and eel, you can finish it as ochazuke (green tea over rice), which is characteristic of hitsumabshi

records.name: MOZU
records.menu: otsumami (finger foods) set menu, potato salad, dashimaki tamago (rolled omelet), tataki kyuuri (smashed cucumber salad), oshinko moriawase (assorted Japanese pickled vegetables), daikon sarada (radish salad), negi toro maki (sushi diced tuna with green onion), sunagimo (gizzard), nankotsu (chicken cartilage), seseri (grilled chicken neck), tebasaki (deep-fried chicken wings), momo (dumplings), udon, soba (Japanese buckwheat noodles)
records.description: This is a great place to have a drink along with the set menu of otsumami (Izakaya-style side dishes). You can also order à la carte and choose from a wide variety of skewers and Japanese snacks. This branch in Busan was opened by Chef Yokomori, who is also the owner of Mozu, a popular restaurant in Sinsa-dong, Seoul.

records.name: SHOJIN
records.description: Here, you can enjoy Japanese kaiseki (multicourse set menu). They use seasonal, high-quality ingredients, including geumtae (blackthroat seaperch), tuna, sea urchin roe, sweet shrimp, and beef. The meal is served in small portions, allowing you to try a variety of dishes, including sashimi, suimono (broth), soba (buckwheat noodles), grilled dishes, and rice cooked in an iron pot.

records.name: Sushi sian
records.hours: First seating 6:00 p.m. - 8:00 p.m. / Second seating 8:00 p.m. - 10:00 p.m.
records.description: This sushi restaurant offers sushi omakase (chef's choice) and is run by a solo chef. Dinner omakase is served in two sittings, only in the evening. Some people find the taste of the shari (vinegared rice) to be a bit strong, but others prefer it. Overall, the restaurant offers good value for the price.

records.name: SUSHI IRUKA
records.hours: Lunch: 12 a.m to 2 p.m. / Dinner: First seating from 5:30 p.m., Second seating from 8:00 p.m.
records.description: This sushi omakase (chef's choice) restaurant offers great value for the price. The shari (vinegared rice) made with akazu red vinegar pairs perfectly with rich-tasting fish like aji (horse mackerel) and saba (blue mackerel).

records.name: YAKITORI Haegong
records.menu: yakitori omakase (chef's choice chicken skewers), chicken skewers, tsukune (japanese chicken meatball skewer), saengyachae boridoenjang (barley doenjang with fresh vegetables), chaeso gui (grilled vegetables), dak bong croquettes (chicken drumsticks croquettes), saeusisomari chungwon twigim (shrimp spring rolls with perilla leaves), cheese gui (grilled cheese)
records.description: This yakitori restaurant with a lavish decor is renowned for its yakitori omakase (chef's choice chicken skewers) made with domestically-raised chickens. You can try almost every part of the chicken, including the tenderloin, neck, oyster, Achilles tendon, thigh, wing, leg, and skin.

records.name: Zero Base
records.description: Here, they serve Japanese omakase (chef's choice) as a single course. Savor the genuine taste of the finest ingredients, such as fresh wasabi and sea urchin from Hokkaido. Various sake and tokuri (traditional sake flask) are also available to complement the dishes.

records.name: TETE O NE
records.hours:
3:00 p.m. - 12:00 a.m. (Last order 11:00 p.m.) | SAT 12:00 p.m. - 12:00 a.m. (Last order 11:00 p.m.) | SUN 12:00 p.m. - 6:00
p.m. (Last order 5:00 p.m.)
records.description: This is a wine bar with a casual and lively atmosphere. Beef tartare, French-style minced raw beef, is a popular menu item and is served with baguette. Pasta is also available on the lunch menu. Liquor or soft drinks must be ordered with food.

records.name: La ConTi
records.menu: dinner course, saengmyeon pasta (fresh pasta), chaekkeut deungsim steak (striploin steaks)
records.description: At this restaurant, you can enjoy high-quality Italian cuisine. It is known for its fresh pasta, which is made daily in-house. The wood-fired oven pizza and steak are also highly recommended. The set menu, which consists of a variety of dishes, is also very satisfying.

records.name: Rione
records.menu: salad, seonggeal eoran pasta (sea urchin & cured fish roe pasta), chorizo aglio e olio pasta, tomato ragu oven panne pasta, algamja gnocchi (baby potatoes gnocchi)
records.description: This casual Italian restaurant is known for its delicious gnocchi. The potato-shaped gnocchi are perfectly paired with a rich truffle-and-cream sauce. The small garden in front of the entrance is a lovely touch.

records.name: Chef Lee
records.menu: aglio e olio pasta, cacio e pepe pasta, anchovy pasta, gorgonzola cheese pizza, prosciutto pizza, rucola pizza (arugula pizza), gambas al ajillo, maeun honghap jjim (spicy braised mussels), hanu chaekkeut (Korean beef strip loin)
records.description: This Italian restaurant sticks to the basics, and the pasta dishes are the most popular items on the menu. The pizza is baked in an Italian woodfired oven, and you can taste the freshness of the ingredients. You can also enjoy Italian beer, which is not easily found elsewhere.

records.name: Osteria Aboo
records.address: 3F, The Sailing Tower, 23 Haeundae-ro 570beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
records.menu: oyster, tongbal dansaeu (wild-caught sweet shrimp), Jeju san chamokdom (Jeju red tilefish), muneo risotto (octopus risotto), osso buco risotto, carbonara pasta, Itallia gajae pasta (Italian lobster pasta), bollonyasik sogogi pasta (bolognese pasta), hanu two plus chaekkeut steak (hanu strip loin steak)
records.description: This is a great place to enjoy Italian cuisine and wine. The ddak-saewoo pasta, which harmonizes red-banded lobster from Jeju and linguine noodles, and the classic carbonara are popular dishes, and the osso buco risotto with tender veal is also highly recommended.

records.name: Lee Jae-mo Pizza
records.menu: crust pizza, ham cheese crust pizza, crust saeu pizza (shrimp pizza), pepperoni pizza, pasta
records.description: This pizza place is a local favorite, known for its delicious cheese. Their pepperoni pizza is popular. You can upgrade your pizza to a larger size for an additional 4000 won. Be prepared to wait, as it can get busy.

records.name: Restaurant L’étang
records.hours: 12:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. / 6:00 p.m. - 9:00 p.m. (By reservation only)
records.description: This restaurant offers French set menus that combine the chef's experience in France and Japan. The set menu changes seasonally according to what ingredients are locally available. The restaurant has a counter-style layout and is operated by a single chef, so reservations are essential. You can enjoy classic French dishes like escargot and rabbit at reasonable prices. There is also a diverse wine selection, so this is a good place for a glass of wine.

records.name: RAEOAK
records.menu: sogogi ssalguksu (beef rice noodles), Raeok pho ga (Raeok chicken pho), haemul bokkeumbap (seafood fried rice), banh xeo (crispy Vietnamese crêpes), goi cuon (cool shrimp, pork, or beef rice wraps), banh quay (fried breadstick), bunmangbit (Vietnamese duck vermicelli noodle soup), bun bo hue (spicy neef & pork noodle soup)
records.description: The staff at this restaurant learned at Lai Ngọc, a rice noodle restaurant in Hanoi, Vietnam. They offer beef noodle soup with a clean-tasting broth. The bánh xèo is filled generously and also recommended. The interior, which recreates the atmosphere of the original restaurant, is also impressive.

records.name: DAL THAI
records.menu: poo pad pong curry (stir-fried crab and curry powder), tom yum goong (hot and sour prawn soup),pad thai (Thai stir-fried rice noodles with meat and vegetables), green curry, red curry, som tam thai (Thai spicy green papaya salad), khao pad nea (beef fried rice), khao pad kung (shrimp fried rice), pat gra-prao moo sap (stir-fried minced pork), kao ka moo (braised pork trotters), quay tiew tom yum (tom yum noodle soup)
records.description: This Thai restaurant's poo pad pong curry and tom yum goong are renowned. Here, you can enjoy authentic Thai cuisine. The food is even better when paired with Thai beer. The interior has been renovated and became modern and stylish.

records.name: ALOI THAI RESTAURANT
records.menu: poo pad pong curry (stir-fried crab and curry powder), poo nim pad pong curry (crispy fried soft-shell crab with curry powder), Thai sik haemul ssalguksu (Thai seafood rice noodles), pineapple bokkeumbap (pineapple fried rice), yum woon sen (Thai seafood and rice noodle salad), Aroi appetizer set menu
records.description: This is a premium "Thai Select" restaurant, certified by the Thai government. You can savor authentic Thai cuisine prepared by a chef from a hotel in Thailand. Especially popular dishes are the poo pad pong curry, made with crab and fresh cream, and the fried rice with plenty of fresh pineapple.

records.name: Cappadocia
records.menu: kebab, pirzola (lamb chops), pita, lunch set, Cappadocia special (set menu including ekmek, lavash, and kebabs)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in Turkish cuisine, which is rare in Busan. You can taste various authentic Turkish dishes, including kebabs. Various types of kebabs are popular, and the grilled pirzola (lamb ribs marinated in traditional spices) is also recommended. The restaurant is owned and operated by a Turkish immigrant, and traditional Turkish handicrafts are displayed throughout the store.

records.name: Geobukseon hoetjip
records.menu: jayeonsan modum hoe (assorted sliced raw wild fish)
records.description: This sashimi restaurant is located in Mipo, Haeundae. It is well known for its excellent wildcaught sashimi, as well as its various side dishes and maeuntang (spicy fish stew). The secret to the delicious taste is their chojang, a sauce made by mixing various seasonings with red pepper paste that has been aged for six months. This restaurant is a favorite of former President Moon Jae-in.

records.name: Goseurak
records.menu: hanu deungsim gui (grilled Korean beef sirloin), hanu ansim (Korean beef tenderloin), hanu tteokgalbi sotbap jeongsik (grilled Korean galbi patties with hot stone pot rice)
records.description: This bungalow restaurant on the beach offers a stunning view and quality beef. A special feature is that it is dog-friendly. After your meal, it's nice to take a stroll along the beach.

records.name: Gyuujeong
records.menu: chaekkeut (striploin), ansim (grilled tenderloin), deungsim (grilled sirloin), kkotdeungsim (ribeye), teuk ansim (beef tenderloin), assorted grilled Korean beef cuts (rib-eye, tenderloin, brisket), omurice (rice-filled omelet)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in grilled beef and offers a stunning view of the ocean. When you order meat, you will be served basic side dishes and three seasonings: salt, sesame oil, and demi-glace. The aged meat is flavorful, and the omurice with demiglace is also a satisfying meal on its own.

records.name: Geumnang hoetjip
records.menu: Geumnang hansang (raw fish full-course), Subyeon hansang, Gwangan hansang (raw fish full-course), Bada hansang, teuk modum hoe (assorted sliced raw fish special), modum hoe (assorted sliced raw fish)
records.description: At this restaurant located in Gwangalli Waterside Park, you can enjoy a Korean table setting while taking in the views of Gwangan Bridge. They serve fresh sashimi, as well as plentiful side dishes including maeuntang (spicy fish stew), steamed abalone, mero (toothfish) steak, assorted seafood, and shrimp sauce. This restaurant was visited by former President Moon Jae-in.

records.name: NEWLY
records.menu: vongole pasta (clam pasta), formaggi pasta, chaekkeut steak (striploin steaks), ansim steak (tenderloin steak), gamja twigim (french fries), lunch set, dinner set
records.description: This steakhouse offers a stunning view of Gwangalli Sea and offers an à-la-carte menu. At lunch, a set menu is available that includes salad, pasta, Korean beef steak, and dessert. In the evening, it transforms into a wine bar.

records.name: McQUEEN'S Lounge
records.menu: afternoon tea set, black tea, herbal tea, gwasil cha (fruit tea), nokcha (green tea), jeontongcha (traditional Korean tea), espresso, Americano, cappuccino, caffe latte, caffe mocha, vanilla latte
records.description: This lounge is located in the Ananti Hilton Busan. It is a place to enjoy dessert and tea while taking in the fantastic ocean view. The signature menu items are their baked goods, which include cakes, and the afternoon tea set with a selection of signature teas.

records.name: Mokjangwon
records.menu: hanu deungsim (grilled Korean beef sirloin), hanu yangnyeom gui (grilled marinated Korean beef), hanu kkotdeungsim (Korean beef ribeye steak), yangnyeom galbitsal (grilled marinated boneless galbi), kkotgalbisal sogeumgui (grilled boneless galbi), hanu teuksubuwi modum (assorted special cuts of Korean beef), hanu kkotgalbisal (boneless Korean galbi), hanu gomtang (Korean beef bone soup), galbitang (galbi soup)
records.description: At this restaurant specializing in charcoal-grilled beef ribs, you can enjoy Korean and imported beef. Take in the stunning views of Taejongdae as you dine. You can also enjoy a cup of tea at Café de Bom on the second floor, or make use of the banquet hall or outdoor wedding hall.

records.name: Oryukdogawon
records.menu: galbitsal (grilled boneless galbi), deungsim (grilled sirloin), jebichuri (beef neck chain), kkotsal (grilled boneless short ribs)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in Korean beef and offers great views of the sea. The Korean beef is high-quality and is grilled over charcoal, giving it a delicious flavor. If you order grilled Korean beef during lunchtime, rice and naengmyeon (cold noodles in chilled broth or spicy sauce) are included. The restaurant's exterior, which artfully blends water features and lawns, is so beautiful that it won an architectural award. There is also a café next door, which is a great place to enjoy a cup of tea after your meal.

records.name: Ireok
records.menu: gomtang (beef bone soup), yanggomtang (beef tripe soup), teuk seokkeo gomtang (beef bone soup with beef tripe), suyuk (boiled pork slices)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in gomtang, a light and refreshing soup made with Korean beef. Their yang-gomtang (beef soup with smooth tripe) is also a popular menu item. The terrace offers stunning views of Gwangan Bridge.

records.name: Chilseong hoetjip
records.menu: dodari sekkosi (bone-in sliced raw ridged-eye flounder), ureok (rockfish), gwangeo (flatfish), jabeo (small fish), sea bream, gwangeo tongmari (whole flatfish)
records.description: This restaurant is a great place to enjoy sekkosi (chopped raw small fish) while taking in the view of Gwangan Bridge. The secret of this restaurant's great-tasting food is the ssamjang (spicy soybean paste) that is served with the sekkosi. You can get high-quality sekkosi at a reasonable price, and the maeuntang (spicy seafood stew) made in an earthenware pot is also excellent.

records.name: Nampung
records.menu: jeomsim course (full-course lunch set menu) , chef's signature course , special full-course set menu , buldojang (Buddha's temptation soup), eojahaesamsongi (fried Korean sea cucumber and pine mushroom)
records.description: Nampoong Chinese Restaurant has been a wellknown high-end Chinese restaurant in Busan for many years. It reinterprets traditional Cantonese Chinese cuisine in a Korean style. Their signature dishes include fried Korean sea cucumber, Cantonese veal ribs, and buldojang ('BuddhaJumps-Over-the-Wall' soup), all made with their own recipes. The restaurant is located on the third floor of the new building of Paradise Hotel, and offers stunning views of the ocean.

records.name: LABXXIV by KUmuda
records.menu: lunch full-course set menu, dinner course
records.hours: 12:00 p.m. - 3:00 p.m. / 5:30 p.m. - 10:00 p.m. (By reservation only)
records.description: LAB XXIV Kumuda is a high-end French restaurant run by Chef Edward Kwon. Enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of Songjeong Beach and refined full-course set menus at reasonable prices in a luxurious atmosphere. It is located on the fourth floor of the Kumuda Multiple Cultural Experience Space.

records.name: Le DORER
records.description: You can enjoy set menus and stunning night views in this modern Korean cuisine bar with a luxurious atmosphere. It serves set menus including a wide variety of seasonal seafood, such as octopus, eel, and yellowtail.

records.name: Michael's Urban Farm Table
records.menu: full-course business set menu, Michael's course, salad, pasta, sandwich & burger, coconut shrimp, grilled calamari
records.description: This American restaurant serves American-style dishes made with seasonal ingredients from Busan. Fajitas, truffle spaghetti, and Michael's signature burger are all recommended menu items. We highly recommend the outdoor terrace seats, which offer stunning night views of Busan. It is located in F1963, a multicultural complex.

records.name: Mori
records.description: This restaurant offers a Japanese kaiseki dining experience with a view of Haeundae Beach. The authentic interior and staff's yukata (cotton kimono) create an immersive Japanese atmosphere. You can enjoy a wide range of dishes, from sashimi prepared with fresh seasonal ingredients, to suimono (broth), tempura, grilled dishes, and rice cooked in an iron pot. It is located on the second floor of Palé de Cz.

records.name: Mugunghwa
records.menu: course menu, hanu bulgogi bansang (bulgogi set menu)
records.description: Located on the forty-third floor of Lotte Hotel Busan, this elegant Korean restaurant offers a panoramic view of Baekyang Mountain. They serve traditional cuisine for the nobility that has been reinterpreted as Korean set menus with a modern touch, making it popular with both Koreans and foreigners. The restaurant also has a wine list that pairs well with Korean food, as well as halal dishes for Muslims

records.name: SAKAE
records.menu: course menu, set, cheolpan course (griddled dish course)
records.description: Located in Paradise Hotel, this Japanese restaurant serves authentic, high-quality cuisine made with fresh ingredients. The sushi counter is a popular choice, as is the teppanyaki, which highlights the natural flavors of the ingredients.

records.name: Sheobul
records.menu: course menu, hanu bulgalbi (grilled marinated Korean beef), hanu yukhoe bibimbap (Korean beef tartare bibimbap), hanu tteokgalbi bansangcharim (grilled Korean galbi patties set menu)
records.description: This long-standing Korean restaurant in the Westin Chosun Busan Hotel serves traditional Korean cuisine with sincerity. Its banquet hall, which has a view of Haeundae, is a popular place for important events.

records.name: Â POINT
records.menu: lunch full-course set menu, dinner course
records.description: This restaurant offers course set menus, which you can enjoy while taking in the view of the open sea. The course set menu consists of eight dishes, all of which is French cuisine with a Korean twist. The highlight of the meal is the steak, which is followed by a combination of Korean side dishes. The fish dishes included in the set menu change seasonally. Reservations are required.

records.name: AOMORI
records.description: This Japanese restaurant located in the Centum Hotel offers high-quality sashimi. If you order a set menu, the sashimi is followed by a variety of seafood, vegetables and scallops, grilled beef, and then rice, soup, and side dishes. The sushi set menu is also popular, and the sake list is excellent too.

records.name: Yulling
records.menu: course menu, special full-course set menu, hanu gui (grilled Korean beef), glass wine pairing
records.description: This Korean beef restaurant offers a luxurious dining experience with a stunning ocean view of Haeundae. Enjoy omakase (chef's choice) Korean beef dishes combining Japanese and French style. The restaurant has counter seats, several private rooms, and a large wine cellar.

records.name: CHAORAN
records.menu: lunch set , dinner set, Chaoran's Peking duck, dim sum selection
records.description: This is a Chinese restaurant located in the Signiel Hotel in Busan. They offer modern Cantonese cuisine in a setting inspired by 1920s Hong Kong. During the day, you can enjoy dim sum and tea, while the evening hours are perfect for cocktails at the bar

records.name: PALAIS DE CHINE
records.menu: lunch full-course set menu, dinner course, bukgyeong ori (Peking duck), Ibérico chashu, basakhan samgyeopsal barbecue (crispy barbecued pork belly), jeonbog yangjangpi (abalone starch sheet salad with mustard sauce), buldojang (Buddha's temptation soup), sacheonsik laziji (Sichuan spicy chicken with eggplant), hunyeonhyang mero (smoked patagonian toothfish)
records.description: This modern Chinese restaurant in the Grand Josun Busan hotel has a panoramic ocean view. Their Peking duck is definitely the standout dish, while chili shrimp with Shaoxing wine and smoked grouper are also popular choices. You can also enjoy signature dishes from Hongyeon in the Westin Josun, such as buldojang ('Buddha-JumpsOver-the-Wall' soup) and tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork). The Peking duck must be ordered at least two days in advance.

records.name: palate
records.menu: lunch full-course set menu, dinner course
records.description: This French restaurant claims to be a neobistro. From amuse-bouches to appetizers and main courses, the dishes are beautifully plated and made with high-quality ingredients. The restaurant started as a wine bar, so wine pairing is highly recommended.

records.name: HAREMA
records.menu: lunch set, dinner, first seating , dinner, second seating
records.description: Here, they serve sushi omakase (chef's choice) made with fresh, high-quality seasonal ingredients. In the dinner course set menu, more than ten kinds of tsumami (Japanese hors d'oeuvres) are offered first. Served on a Dior plate, their signature dish is tuna, sea urchin, and avocado mousse, which is wrapped in laver before eating. They serve Mazuma wasabi that they bring in by air from Shizuoka and grate just before serving.

records.name: Yuksimnyeon jeontong  halmaegukbap
records.menu: dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), naejang gukbap (offal and rice soup), guksu (noodles), ttaro gukbap (rice and soup), suybaek (boiled pork slices set menu), suyuk (boiled pork slices)
records.description: This restaurant is famous for its Busan-style dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice) with Chinese chives. The soup is clear and refreshing, and the taste is enhanced by adding plenty of Chinese chives. 'Subaek' means suyuk-baekban, which is rice and pork soup with the boiled pork slices and sundae (Korean sausage) served on the side

records.name: Gaegeum milmyeon
records.menu: mul milmyeon (cold wheat noodles) , bibim milmyeon (spicy wheat noodles), Gaegeum mandu , gogigomyeong (meat garnish), hoegomyeong chuga (extra sliced raw fish garnish)
records.description: This restaurant has been serving milmyeon (wheat noodles) for over fifty years, making it one of the oldest milmyeon restaurants, along with Gaya Milmyeon. The noodles are made with a combination of wheat flour and sweet potato starch, which gives them their characteristic chewy texture. In the summer, expect to wait in line for a table.

records.name: Gupochonguksu
records.description: This restaurant specializes in just one thing: myeolchi guksu (noodles in anchovy broth). When you order noodles, you will be served boiled noodles and a kettle of broth, and you can pour as much broth as you like over the noodles. The broth is prepared by simmering anchovies from the southern coast of Korea. It is best enjoyed with plenty of chopped Cheongyang peppers. This restaurant is considered to be the originator of Gupo noodles.

records.name: Geumsubokguk
records.menu: bok guk (puffer fish soup), bok twigim (deep-fried puffer fish), bokkkeopjil twigim (fried puffer fish skin) , bok kkeopjil muchim (puffer fish skin salad), bok jjim (braised puffer fish), bok suyuk (boiled puffer fish slices), bok sashimi (sliced raw puffer fish)
records.description: This is the oldest bokguk restaurant in the Haeundae area. Bokguk (pufferfish soup) is Busan's representative hangover soup, and a bowl of clear jiri bokguk completely cures a hangover. The spicy bokmaeuntang is also popular, but if you want to enjoy cleantasting pufferfish, the jiri bokguk is recommended. On the second floor, they offer a variety of pufferfish course set menus.

records.name: Geumyong
records.menu: mul mandu (boiled mandu), jjin mandu (steamed mandu), gun mandu (pan-fried mandu), mandu gukbap (mandu rice soup)
records.description: This is a place where you can enjoy handmade, oldfashioned steamed dumplings. It is run by an ethnic Chinese. The dumplings are made fresh daily, so they are juicy and flavorful. Fried dumplings are also a popular menu item, and mandu gukbap (dumpling soup and rice) is recommended for a full meal. You can feel the passion that has gone into making dumplings for over 50 years. Please note that fried dumplings are only available after 10:30 AM.

records.name: Gijang gomjangeo
records.menu: gomjangeo (inshore hagfish (straw fire-grilled, grilled marinated, grilled whole, or salt-grilled)), gomjangeo maeuntang (spicy inshore hagfish stew), gomjangeo doenjangguk (inshore hagfish soybean paste soup)
records.description: This restaurant is the originator of grilling Gijang gomjangeo (sea eel from Gijang) over a straw fire. After the sea eel has been moderately grilled over a straw fire, you can peel off the charred skin to reveal the golden brown flesh, which you can cut in bite-size pieces and dip in sesame oil or salt. You can have pine needle sea eel, which imparts an aromatic flavor, and sea eel doenjangguk (bean paste soup), which has a savory flavor.

records.name: Dongnae halmaepajeon
records.menu: Dongnae pajeon (Dongnae green onion pancake), Dongnae godong jjim (steamed sea snails), yakcho jeonbyeong muchim (medicinalherb buckwheat pancake and duck salad), samsaek deodeok gui (grilled deodeok root), golbaengi muchim (sea snail salad), Ttugisang (set menu), Ttumisang (set menu)
records.description: This restaurant has been in business for over eighty years and has been passed down through four generations. It is famous for its pajeon, which is a thick green onion pancake that is hearty enough to be a meal on its own. The pajeon has a rich flavor and is made with a mixture of various seafood, including clams, shrimp, oysters, mussels, and other seafood and fried in rapeseed oil. The restaurant also offers a popular Korean table setting menu, which includes pajeon, braised godong-jjim (steamed seasoned turban shells), golbaengi-muchim (moon snail salad), and deodeok-gui (grilled lance asiabell root).

records.name: Mulkkong sikdang
records.menu: agwi jjim (spicy braised monkfish), agwi suyuk (boiled monkfish slices), agwi tang (monkfish soup)
records.description: This restaurant has been making agui-jjim (braised spicy monkfish) for over 60 years. They use only fresh monkfish, so their agui-jjim has a clean taste and a refreshing aftertaste. The scent and taste of their agui-jjim may be unfamiliar because it contains Korean mint leaves, which are eaten by people from Gyeongsang-do.

records.name: puffer fish soup
records.menu: bok guk (puffer fish soup), bok maeuntang (spicy puffer fish stew), eunbok suyuk (boiled brown-backed toadfish slices), daegutang (codfish soup)
records.description: Here, you can enjoy clean-tasting bokguk (pufferfish soup). The key to making bokguk is to use enough meat and prepare a flavorful broth, and this restaurant is known for its delicious bokguk with a rich, concentrated broth. The restaurant is small but popular, so you may have to wait in line during lunchtime.

records.name: Bae Jong-gwan Dongnae  samgyetang
records.menu: Dongnae samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), gungjung yakgyetang (chicken soup with medicinal herbs)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in samgyetang (chickenginseng soup) and has only two items on the menu: goong-joong yakgyetang (royal chicken soup with medicinal herbs) and Dongnae samgyetang. The soup is made with a large chicken, and the broth is rich and flavorful. A glass of ginseng wine is served before the soup, which is topped with green onions. The restaurant is popular and often has a long line of customers.

records.name: Baekgudang
records.menu: Baekgu pie (109-layered pastry with custard-cream filling), croizen (soft roll filled with corn salad), ssuk ssal sikppang (mugwort rice loaf bread), bluebarry sikppang (blueberry loaf bread), pat donut (donut with red bean filling), Italian croquette, chapssal pat donut (sweet rice red bean donut), baguette pizza, yachae ppang (vegetable bun), sausage pastry
records.description: This bakery in Busan has been in operation for over 60 years. The most popular item is their croizen, a soft roll filled with corn salad. They also sell a variety of other simple but delicious oldfashioned kinds of bread that are popular with those who have fond memories of them.

records.name: Busan myeongmul hoetjip
records.menu: hoe baekban (sliced raw fish set menu), hoe bibimbap (raw fish bibimbap), mulhoe (cold raw fish soup), jeonbok juk (abalone rice porridge), dom meori tang (sea bream head stew), saengseon yangnyeomgui (grilled marinated fish head)
records.description: This 80-year-old hoe-baekban-jip (sashimi restaurant) is located in Jagalchi Market. The generous portions of thick-cut sashimi, the chojang (sour and spicy dipping sauce), and the side dishes are all tantalizing. Their hoebaekban (sashimi set meal) comes with a plate of sashimi, rice, clear fish soup, and five or six side dishes. Depending on the season, salted fish intestines, salted rockfish, and crab sauce are also served.

records.name: B&C
records.menu: Busanae ppang (bread with sweet potato and cream cheese filling), croissant, French pie, mini castella, sangtu gwaja (white bean paste cookies), choco muffin, cheese muffin, pain de gênes, Mont Blanc bread, soboru ppang (Korean streusel bun), ttalgi saengkeurim mini cake (strawberry mini cake with whipped cream)
records.description: This old bakery in Busan has been in business for over 40 years. Their popular menu items include the salad bun with potato-salad filling and pie manju. In addition to traditional breads, they also offer Mont Blancs and egg tarts.

records.name: Saejinju sikdang
records.menu: yukhoe bibimbap (beef tartare bibimbap), dolsot bibimbap (hot stone pot bibimbap), hoe bibimbap (raw fish bibimbap), seoksoe bulgogi (grilled bulgogi), yukhoe (beef tartare), gaori muchim (spicy ray salad), pajeon (green onion pancake)
records.description: This 70-year-old restaurant serves Jinju-style yukhoe bibimbap, a dish made with fresh raw beef and various vegetables that are evenly mixed together. When you order the bibimbap, they also serve seonjitguk (hangover soup with oxblood) and mul kimchi (water kimchi), which are delicacies. Other menu items include grilled bulgogi, pajeon (green-onion pancakes), and gaori-muchim (seasoned raw stingray).

records.name: Seoul kkakdugi
records.menu: seolleongtang (ox bone soup), gomtang (beef bone soup), yangjitang (brisket and flank soup), suyuk (boiled pork slices)
records.description: This restaurant has been serving seolleongtang (ox-bone soup) for over eighty years. Seolleongtang is a popular dish in Seoul, but it has also won over the taste buds of Busan residents. The restaurant only serves two side dishes, kimchi and kkakdugi (radish kimchi), but the flavor is excellent.

records.name: Songjeong samdae gukbap
records.menu: dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), sundae gukbap (sundae and rice soup), naejang gukbap (offal and rice soup), ttaro gukbap (rice and soup), suyuk baekban (boiled pork slices set menu), chapssal sundae (sweet rice sundae), suyuk (boiled pork slices)
records.description: This restaurant's dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice) is made from the best cuts of pork and is milky and clean-tasting. Another popular item is their chapssal-sundae (Korean sausage), which is made with glutinous rice instead of cellophane noodles. They have been in business for 80 years and are one of the original restaurants in Seomyeon's "dwaeji-gukbap Alley.

records.name: Sinbarwon
records.menu: gogi mandu (meat mandu), jjin gyoja (steamed dumplings), gun mandu (pan-fried mandu), maepgun (spicy seasoned fried mandu), saeu gyoza (shrimp dumplings), mala mandu
records.description: This restaurant is well-known for its Chinese dumplings, which have a thick yet soft skin and a well-balanced filling of ginger and pork. In addition to Chinese dumplings, they also specialize in Chinese breads such as pat-bbang (red-bean bread) and dalgyal-bbang (egg bread). Bean soup, which is a popular breakfast food in China, is served with snacks. This restaurant has a history of over 70 years.

records.name: Sinchan ggukbap
records.menu: This place serves dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice), which has a refreshing and savory flavor. It also serves well-cooked suyuk (steamed pork) and sundae (Korean sausage) in generous portions. This place is located in Nampo-dong International Market and has become a popular tourist destination in Busan because of its delicious food.
records.description: This place serves dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice), which has a refreshing and savory flavor. It also serves well-cooked suyuk (steamed pork) and sundae (Korean sausage) in generous portions. This place is located in Nampo-dong International Market and has become a popular tourist destination in Busan because of its delicious food.

records.name: Sinheunggwan
records.menu: jjajangmyeon (noodles in black bean sauce), udon, jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup), tangsuyuk (deep-fried pork with sweet and sour sauce), kkanpunggi (sweet and spicychicken)
records.description: This 70-year-old restaurant specializes in Sichuan Chinese cuisine. Popular menu items include the jajang-myeon (noodles and Sichuan sauce with a fiery, smoky flavor) and classic tangsuyuk (sweet-and-sour beef or pork) with large chunks of cucumber, carrots, and jelly ear mushrooms. In addition, they serve delicious kkanpunggi (spicy garlic fried chicken).

records.name: Yennal omakjip
records.menu: teuk yang (ox tripe), daechang (grilled beef large intestines), gopchang (grilled beef small intestines / grilled pork small intestines), baekteugyang (grilled beef tripe special), yeomtong (grilled thinly-sliced beef heart), kongpat (beef kidneys)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in yang (smooth tripe) and gopchang (small intestine) and has over 60 years of tradition. Korean beef smooth tripe and small intestines are marinated in homemade sesame oil and marinade, and then grilled over charcoal. The smooth tripe, and small and large intestines are all of high quality, and the seasoning complements the flavors perfectly. The seasoning sauce is Gyeongsang-do style, made by mixing red pepper powder and starch syrup. The smooth-tripe fried rice is also delicious.

records.name: Wonjo halmaenakji
records.menu: nakji bokkeum (spicy stir-fried octopus), nakji saeu bokkeum (spicy stir-fried shrimp and octopus), nakji sogopchang bokkeum (spicy stir-fried beef intestines and octopus), nakji saeu sogopchang bokkeum (spicy stir-fried Shrimp, beef intestines, and octopus, sari (side order)
records.description: This restaurant has been serving nakji-bokkeum (stir-fried octopus) for over 50 years. This is nakjibokkeum, but their version contains broth, so it's more like jeongol (hot pot). The variation with beef small intestine is also recommended. The nakjibokkeum can be mixed with rice or boiled with udon noodles.

records.name: Chowonbokguk
records.menu: bok guk (puffer fish soup), bok bulgogi (puffer fish bulgogi), bok course (pufferfish full-course set menu)
records.description: This restaurant is renowned for its pufferfish cuisine and has been handed down for two generations over the past 60 years. You can choose from a variety of pufferfish dishes, such as bokchiri (clear pufferfish soup) and bok-maeuntang (spicy pufferfish soup), and you can choose the pufferfish you want. When you order a pufferfish full course set menu, you will be served pufferfish prepared a variety of ways: as shabu-shabu, deep-fried, in a sweet-and-sour salad, and as a porridge. It is so popular that there are branches all over Busan.

records.name: Pyeongsanok
records.menu: suyuk (boiled pork slices), guksu (noodles), yeolmu guksu (young summer radish kimchi noodles)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in dwaeji-suyuk (boiled pork) and has a 100-year history. The suyuk is served in generous portions. The dwaeji-sagolguksu (pork bone noodle soup) they serve as a meal is a reliable option. Suyuk can also be purchased to take home.

records.name: Halmae jaecheopguk
records.menu: jaecheop guk (marsh clam soup), jaecheop hoe (raw marsh clams)
records.description: This is the original restaurant in Samnakdong's "Jaecheop Alley." Along with an order of jaecheopguk (small clam soup), they serve rice, a large bowl for mixing, braised mackerel, kkakdugi (radish kimchi), kimchi, and doenjang-jjigae (soybean paste stew). The rice mixed with the jaecheop and seasoning goes perfectly with the refreshing soup. The reason their rice tastes so good is that they make their rice in a cast-iron pot.

records.name: Haeundae somunnan amso  galbijip
records.menu: hanu saenggalbi (grilled Korean beef galbi), hanu yangnyeom galbi (grilled marinated Korean galbi), bulgogi, ttukbaegi doenjang (soybean paste jjigae hot pot)
records.description: This restaurant is considered the birthplace of Haeundae-style ribs. Since opening in 1964, it has maintained its reputation for quality. After grilling the meat on the special grill pan shaped like a jeongol (hotpot) pan, you can order potato noodles to add and enjoy it like a hotpot. Because the restaurant is in a hanok (traditional Korean house), you feel like a guest in a nobleman's house. Many celebrities are frequent customers

records.name: lesmains patisserie
records.menu: ttalgi mille-feuille (strawberry mille-feuille), tarte chocolat, orange cocoa madeleine, muhwagwa keurimchijeu financier (fig butter cream cheese financier), Haenam bamgoguma crème brulée (sweet potato crème brulée), Americano, caffe latte
records.description: This place specializes in traditional French pastries, such as madeleines and financiers. The chocolate tarts, which are rich in chocolate, and the millefeuilles are among the most popular menu items. They also have seasonal items, such as strawberry mille-feuilles and chestnut madeleines.

records.name: MUG Dessert LAB
records.menu: Americano, caffe latte, sainthonoré, pistachio Paris-brest , lavender mousse tart with Marco Polo ganache and raspberry, raspberry saint-honoré, masion chocolat éclair
records.description: This is a place where you can indulge in luxuriously plated desserts. The light purple lavender mousse topped with violets is a popular item, and the raspberry jam pairs perfectly with the tart pastry.

records.name: MONSIEUR VINCENT
records.menu: baton, baguette, oat almond, pain au chocolat, croissant, cinnamon roll, olives
records.description: This French-style bakery cafe uses French ingredients, like flour, salt, butter, and chocolate. Their most popular bread is the stick-shaped baton, and a maximum of five can be purchased per person.

records.name: Bonheur Pâtisserie
records.menu: Mont Blanc cake, bûchette, forêt blanche, fraisier, poire caramel (caramel pear cake), canelé, jeorinbae clafouti (clafouti aux poires), caffe allongé, caffe latte, tea
records.description: This dessert café is known for its sweet bread, baked goods, and cakes. They also serve a variety of teas to accompany the desserts. Some of their most popular items include the Mont Blanc and forêt blanche

records.name: bread365
records.menu: croissant, ciabatta, basil meongmul baguette (basil & squid ink baguette), bam sikppang (chestnut loaf bread), tongmil sikppang (whole wheat bread), ttalgi pastry (strawberry pastry), jambon sandwich
records.hours: 11:00 a.m. - 7:30 p.m. (Closed when out of ingredients)
records.description: This bakery offers a variety of baked goods. Their various kinds of baguettes are popular. Their delicately layered croissants and plain bread are also delicious.

records.name: Brilliant
records.menu: Brilliant collection, Brillant grand boîte, madeleine, financier, canelé, gâteaux au citron, galette bretonne, santtalgi hateusyu (raspberry chou)
records.description: This bakery specializes in baked confectioneries and serves traditional French sweets. Pre-ordering is required one day in advance, as they operate primarily with pre-orders and sell out quickly.

records.name: Ops
records.menu: Hagwonjeon (sponge cake), chamchi ppang (stuffed tuna bread), jayeonhyomo ppang (sourdough bread), myeongnan baguette (pollack roe baguette), honey cream cheese, danggeun cake (carrot cake), brioche roll, sogeum ppang (salted butter roll), mascarpone pudding
records.description: This bakery is one of the most popular in Busan and is known for its large, soft, and non-greasy choux cream puffs. Their choux cream puff bread is also gaining popularity and can sell out quickly, so you need to hurry

records.name: Momos
records.menu: hand-drip coffee of the day, Americano, espresso, kangkang (iced coffee with kumquat sherbet), cold brew, caffe latte, seasonal tea, lemon pound cake, croissant, cream brownie, cheese cake
records.description: This coffee shop opened in 2007 as a small takeout store near Oncheonjang Station. One of the founders, barista Jeon Joo-yeon, is the first Korean barista to win two consecutive World Barista Championships. The coffee shop, designed in the style of an old jeoksan gaok (Japanese colonial house), is beautiful, and they recently opened a large-scale roastery and second store in Yeongdo. The signature coffees are their Es Chocolat blend and Fruity Bonbon blend. The coffee shop was also the first in Korea to introduce many coffees from such sources as the Savage Coffee auction in Panama.

records.name: Werk Roasters
records.menu: espresso, Americano filter coffee, caffe latte, cold brew, earl grey, bagel
records.description: Along with Heate, this coffee shop is one of the leaders of the recent specialty-coffee wave in Busan. Coffee roasting, store management, planning, events, and creative activities are popular not only in Busan but also nationwide. The monastery-like store was so popular in the early days that numerous imitation stores appeared nationwide, but after the renovation, the atmosphere became more focused on the coffee itself.

records.name: BLACKUP COFFEE
records.menu: hand-drip coffee, espresso, Americano, yuginong milk tea (organic milk tea), Victoria ttalgi cake (Victoria strawberry cake), malcha chocolat cake (matcha chocolat cake), basil cheese scone, vanilla madeleine, cherry financier
records.description: Along with Momos, this specialty coffee company has come to represent Busan. They operate eight large coffee shops in Busan, Ulsan, and Gyeongnam. The most representative location is the first Blackup coffee shop in Seomyeon, which established Busan's Seomyeon Café Street. Their Blend Coffee Nero has been consistently popular for over ten years. Another favorite is their creative sea salt coffee, which combines cold brew coffee and fresh cream with a pinch of sea salt.

records.name: HYTTE ROASTERY
records.menu: espresso, Americano, caffe latte, flat white, vanilla latte, einspanner, filter coffee, apple and cinnamon ade, apple cinnamon black tea, cupcake (carrot / lemon / blueberry / black tea)
records.description: This coffee shop is a rising star in the specialty coffee boom in Jeonpo-dong. They first opened in the Suyeong area but recently relocated to Jeonpo-dong. This light-roasting coffee shop, along with others like Mesh and Deep Blue Lake, has come to represent Korean coffee. They roast distinctive green coffee beans with clear fruity and floral aromas, and even coffees with a fascinating balance and sweetness are wellrepresented.

records.name: Jyugajeonghyo
records.address: 3F, Haeundae La Muette, 620 Haeundae-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
records.menu: kani (crab), beomgodong saenggang jorim (braised sea snail with ginger), sashimi (sliced raw fish), buri sio tataki (salted chopped yellowtail), hanu kushiage (deep-fried korean beef skewers), kamotsuke somyeon (cold buckwheat noodles dipped in warm duck broth), chamdom ochazuke (sea bream ochazuke), fugu zosui (pufferfish rice soup)
records.description:
Led by Chef Myung Jung-hyo, a pioneering figure in Busan’s Japanese culinary scene, the kaiseki restaurant Juga Jung-hyo makes its long-awaited return.
The restaurant presents a sake-focused, appetizer-driven course designed to maximize harmony with carefully selected sake, with the menu evolving approximately every month to reflect the flow of the seasons.
A signature dish of chilled somen noodles generously infused with freshly ground sesame seeds stands as a defining highlight of the experience.

records.name: Ton shou
records.menu: Berkshire K loseu gaseu (Berkshire K pork sirloin cutlet), loseu gaseu (pork sirloin cutlet), katsu sando (pork cutlet sandwich), modum gaseu (assorted cutlets), ebi gaseu (prawn cutlet)
records.description: This restaurant serves Japanese-style tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet). They make their tonkatsu to order, frying it first at a low temperature, then at a high temperature, and allowing it proper resting time before serving, resulting in meat that is tender, pink, and juicy. Eating it with Maldon salt, the royal salt of the UK, or adding mustard to the special sauce, reduces the greasiness.

records.name: TOBUK BAKERY (토북베이커리)
records.menu:
Signature Rabbit Turtle Coffee (Brewed Americano) ￦5,000
Salt Bread ￦4,000/2
records.description: The cafe has a spacious hanok interior and serves Korean pastry master Kim Deok-gyu’s baked goods. It’s a charming spot where you can look out over the courtyard that blends in with the hanok and enjoy the beauty of the four seasons.

records.name: Cafe Homil (카페호밀)
records.description:
The bakery uses organic flour and naturally leavened sourdough to make its bread. 
Made fresh and sold on the same day, the breads feature French fermented butter, 100% milk fat whipped cream, Madagascar vanilla beans, and cage-free eggs.

records.name: Gohyangyeonhwa
records.description:
It’s a warm and bright restaurant with an exterior that looks like something you’d find at a vacation spot. 
The restaurant is known for its pork cutlet made with premium domestic pork and abalone risotto made with abalones from Wando Island delivered the same day.

records.name: Daeseong  Galchi Jjigaegui
records.menu: Galchi Jjigae (cutlassfish stew) for 1, Galchi Gui (grilled cutlassfish) for 1
records.description: A Daebyeon Port restaurant with many lo-cal regulars that serves stewed and grilled galchi (cutlassfish), anchovy sliced raw fish, and jjigae (stew). The dishes are made of fresh raw anchovies and raw cutlass fish from Jeju Island, with chunky volume and tender flavor.

records.name: Mujinjang Hoetjip Gijang Branch (무진장횟집 기장점)
records.menu:
Conger eel platter(2 servings) ￦60,000
Rock bream platter(2 servings) (market price)
records.description: At this conger eel restaurant, the chef carefully checks the condition of the eel 365 days a year and takes charge of cleaning and cooking. It makes everything on the menu, from the secret sauce to the kimchi.

records.name: Olbareut Main Branch(올바릇 본점)
records.menu:
Kkomak plater ￦38,000
Kkomak and yukjeon platter ￦37,000
records.description:
Bareut Sikdang is a popular restaurant with more than 1,000 visitors per day.
