It offers kkomak bibimbap with special sauce, yukjeon, and other dishes using only domestic ingredients that are served in a unique style. Expect a queue when you are there.

records.name: Alcheon Sundae Gopchang Jeongeol Jeonmunjeom (알천순대곱창전골 전문점)
records.menu:
Sundae Gopchang Hot Pot for 2
(minimum 2 servings) ￦35,000
records.description: From the handmade sundae with ingredients sourced directly from the farm to the hand-cut gopchang, everything here is done with care. With the rich broth and mild flavor of the hot pot, the restaurant attracts a wide range of customers, from college students to the middle-aged.

records.name: Taehwa Banjeom (태화반점)
records.address:
#109, Building B, Hilltop Top Place,
115, Bunpo-ro, Nam-gu
records.menu:
Guangdong-style Sweet and Sour Pork ￦22,000
Sichuan-style Mapo Tofu ￦13,000
records.description: A different style of Chinese cuisine that combines Korean and Japanese styles of Chinese cuisine. It is known for the Cantonese hot and sour pork with ketchup sauce and Japanese-style Sichuan mapo tofu.

records.name: Gongdam
records.description: Serving up trendy dishes by chefs from Seoul’s hottest spots, you’ll find authentic, fresh Italian pasta and brick oven-fired pizzas rested for 72 hour.

records.name: Bae Jong-gwan  Dongnae Samgyetang(배종관동래삼계탕)
records.description:
This restaurant serves samgyetang with a heap of sliced green onions on top.
It uses secret beef bone broth with a 30-year old tradition that boasts deeply nourishing flavors. 
Expect a long queue here as the place is very popular among the locals.

records.name: Singane Hotteok  Gimbap Tteokbokki (신가네 호떡 김밥 떡볶이)
records.description: This 26-year bunsik joint in Dongnae Market is beloved by people of all ages, genders, and even foreign tourists. Ingredients in gimbap, including burdock, are all domestically sourced.

records.name: Cheek to Cheek (칙투칙)
records.description:
The space was opened by a pastry chef who studied and was active in the UK with her sister, a florist. 
It prepares desserts with the flavors of the season, using the best ingredients, and aims to create a place that people want to visit with their loved ones.

records.name: Biscuiterie Française BRILLANT (프랑스 과자점 브리앙)
records.description: Located on the first floor of Bongsikdang, this authentic French patisserie is the shop of a renowned pastry chef. You can find original French sweets with special flavors.

records.name: Gijang  Sonkalguksu
records.description: Known for its hand-kneaded kalguksu noodles, the restaurant serves a rich anchovy broth topped with homemade seasonings and minced garlic.

records.name: Dubeonjjae  Neulhaerang
records.menu:
Steamed pork meal ￦12,000
Pork rice soup ￦9,000
records.description: Famous for its suyukbaekban (steamed pork meal), this second branch of Neulhaerang makes glutinous rice sundae from scratch every day and serves domestic meats, vegetables, and kimchi. It serves sikhae dishes that accompany the meat.

records.name: Werk Roasters (베르크로스터스)
records.description: At Werk Roasters, one can explore a specialty roastery showroom featuring a variety of beans, from espresso to filter coffee, with information and guidance on beans, purchasing, and branded merchandise.

records.name: Cor pasta bar (코르 파스타 바)
records.description:
This fresh pasta restaurant is run by one chef who puts his heart and soul into his dishes, including handmade pasta and bread. It is characterized by a bar-like space 
and a food menu that matches the wine.

records.name: Gombo Sikdang (곰보식당)
records.menu:
Meat from whole ribs ￦29,000
Yukhoe bibimbap ￦15,000
records.description: Established in 1975 and operating for more than 50 years, this Korean beef specialty restaurant has been handling only the best Korean beef cows, which are always selected with experienced expertise. The focus is on bringing out the savory flavor of Korean beef beyond its tenderness.

records.name: 611WoodFire
records.description: This wood-fired restaurant combines the owner’s style with the colors of Busan, creating a unique yet comfortable atmosphere. The smoky aroma from cooking with wood adds to the flavor of the food.

records.name: Golmokpocha
records.menu: LA galbi, Golpo muchim (pork belly with spicy noodles)
records.description:
With a fun name like “drinks prepared by mom,” this is a fun, lively bar with an eclectic menu. 
Every day, people of all ages come here despite the long queues.

records.name: NEWLY
records.description: The meat for the premium ocean-view restaurant in Gwangalli, known for its steaks, was cross-aged for three weeks of wet aging and one week of dry aging to maximize texture and flavor.

records.name: DAIDOKORO (다이도코로)
records.description:
This popular Japanese home-style restaurant offers a variety of local Japanese dishes that are hard to find. 
It continues to work on the menu despite its popularity.

records.name: THE SMOKO
records.menu: Ghee butter tenderloin steak, Scallop cream pasta
records.description:
This restaurant, which looks like it was taken from the streets of Europe, is the first in Korea to grill steak with ghee butter. 
Enjoy brunch and dinner at this sophisticated restaurant with an international staff

records.name: Ramsey (램지)
records.description: The restaurant pursues classic French cuisine and offers different courses for each season using local ingredients from Busan. They also have a professional sommelier on staff with a wide selection of wine glasses.

records.name: MONSIEUR  VINCENT
records.description:
Using French flour and naturally leavened sourdough, the bread is made by the owner, who has been baking bread for 20 years.
It’s so popular that the customers all wait in line before it opens.

records.name: SHABU No.1
records.description: The first place in Korea to make sake-based shabu shabu broth. It is characterized by the use of pork rather than beef, and they use brand meat such as Berkshire K and YBD.

records.name: Outro by Vito (아웃트로 바이 비토)
records.menu:
Sweet shrimp, burrata cheese, vichyssoise, yuja soy jelly ￦17,000
Original ragu, fresh tagliatelle ￦28,000
records.description: This bistro by Chef Vito, who graduated from ICIF in Italy, is the first place in Busan to serve fresh pasta. It offers dishes prepared by a chef with 22 years of experience and natural wines.

records.name: Zerobase (제로베이스)
records.description: This stylish Japanese restaurant offers omakase courses featuring seasonal ingredients, with courses changing monthly. The dishes are prepared using carefully selected ingredients from the fish market and local ingredients from Busan.

records.name: Godeungeodajji Yeonsan Main Branch (고등어다찌 연산본점)
records.menu:
Live mackerel hoe ￦45,000-
Assorted sliced raw fish ￦55,000-
records.description: This is Busan’s first restaurant specializing in live mackerel sliced raw fish. It serves fresh mackerel sliced raw fish by sourcing live mackerel directly from the fishing grounds in Tongyeong.

records.name: Jaegi Dwaejigukbap (재기돼지국밥)
records.description: A famous pork soup restaurant in Yeongdo’s Namhang Market that has been operating for 55 years, the pork soup is served hot in the traditional toryeom style. Customers can customize the meat and other parts to their liking.

records.name: Bubu Coffee
records.menu:
RI drip coffee ￦6,500
Cinnamon island latte ￦7,000
records.description: It is a cozy cafe decorated by a couple who pursue a happy space. It is carefully organized to make guests feel joy with the inhouse dark-roasted specialty coffee.

records.name: Donghwa banjeom
records.menu:
Yuni jjajang ￦8,500
Nanja wans(Korean Chinese meatballs) ￦28,000
records.description: This is the first Chinese restaurant in Busan, founded in 1950. It moved to Bosu-dong in 1987 and also has a store in Namcheon-dong, Nam-gu. It’s been around for a long time, and the quality of food is guaranteed.

records.name: Yeongyeongjae
records.menu:
7:01 AM Blend(시그니처 블렌드) 아메리카노 ￦5,500
달항아리(Dal Hangari) ￦8,000
records.description: Yeongyeongjae operates in a building designed by the founder with a philosophy that expresses the convergence of time, space, and culture. It continues to create and develop coffee drinks, tea, and beverage ingredients from all over the country.

records.name: Myeonok hyangcheon (면옥향천)
records.menu:
Morisoba(when selecting 100% buckwheat) ￦9,000-14,000
Makguksu(when selecting 100% buckwheat) ￦9,000-14,000
records.description: Located at the entrance to the traditional market in U2-dong, this place uses good buckwheat and serves up noodles made with freshly ground flour using millstones and a milling machine. They make their own sauces and are known for croquettes on the side.

records.name: LAB XXIV by Kumuda (랩24 바이 쿠무다)
records.description: Chef Edward Kwon offers his style of French fine dining using Busan ingredients. It is the only restaurant in Busan to be listed in the world’s top 1000 restaurants, “La Liste 1000,” in 2023.

records.name: Le DORER (르도헤)
records.description: It is a modern and creative Korean contemporary restaurant focusing on the ingredients of Busan, offering a unique dining experience with courses that capture the local style and flavors.

records.name: Mori (모리)
records.description: The moment you step inside, you’ll feel the warmth of thoughtful hospitality. This restaurant offers kaiseki-style course meals prepared with the freshest seasonal ingredients, carefully selected daily from the local fish market.

records.name: Bibibidang (비비비당)
records.description: It is a traditional Korean teahouse that uses antique Goryeo celadon and Joseon white porcelain teapots, giving visitors a sense of the past. Through tea time, it presents one with the little leisures in life.

records.name: Sogonggan (소공간)
records.description: Sogonggan, which means both small space and being skilled at cooking beef, is a Korean restaurant that serves 1++-rated beef and features a harmonious composition of local, colorful, and seasonal ingredients sourced on the same day.

records.name: SHOJIN (쇼진)
records.description: Serving omakase courses featuring seasonal ingredients, the restaurant allows for corkage and has rooms for more private dining. It’s a place to experience upscale kaiseki.

records.name: Woobong Shabu Cheongsapo Branch (우봉 샤브 청사포점)
records.menu:
Korean beef brisket shabu shabu (1 person) ￦22,000
Set for 2 ￦67,000
records.description: This premium shabu shabu is made with only the finest 1++-rated beef and is cooked in a paper pot. Everything in sight, including the food served, is neat and carefully organized.

records.name: Chopilsal  Dwaejigui
records.address:
#107, Building A, Byeoksan E Orange Plaza 
23 Marine City 3-ro, Haeundae-gu
records.description: The friendly staff grills the meat for customers. It’s a famous restaurant, and there’s always a wait. Guests can reserve a spot on the Catch Table app. You can customize it with a variety of sauces.

records.name: HAREMA (하레마)
records.address: #106, B1F, Doosan We’ve the Zenith, 33, Marine City 2-ro, Haeundae-gu
records.description: At Harema, the omakase course is served in a private setting. The dinner service is divided into two times, and reservations are 100% required. It is a restaurant with a classy, clean atmosphere.

records.name: Chef Gon
records.address: 12 Junggu-ro 23 beon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan, 48978, South Korea
records.description: Situated in an alley near Jagalchi Market, this joint is run by a former hotel chef with years of experience. Every morning, the chef visits the market to buy fresh ingredients, with which he prepares the day’s seasonal menu.

records.name: ARP
records.address: 35 Taejong-ro 99 beon-gil, Yeongdo-gu, Busan, 49035, South Korea
records.description: ARP offers a 100 percent vegan menu. An acronym formed from the phrase “Around Plants,” the eatery’s name symbolizes the positive, ethical kitchen table of the round Earth and the unlimited possibilities inherent in veggie cuisine.

records.name: Eutteum Iroribata
records.address: 35 Taejong-ro 99 beon-gil, Yeongdo-gu, Busan, 49035, South Korea
records.description: Located near Namcheon station, this Japanese diner specializes in omakase dining prepared using irori (traditional Japanese hearth). Though not as authentic as the ones in old Japanese houses, the irori here is faithful to its role as kitchen equipment.

records.name: Damiok
records.description: Quietly nestled in Gaegeum-dong, Damiok specializes in Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles. As its name suggests, the establishment focuses on presenting refreshingly light and clean flavors.

records.name: Osteria Aboo
records.address: 3F, The Sailing Tower, 23 Haeundae-ro 570beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
records.description: Osteria Aboo first opened in Jeonpo-dong in 2017. Uniquely branded as a “drinking Italian restaurant,” it focuses on authentic Southern Italian cuisine rich in seafood, and relocated to Haeundae-gu in 2026.

records.name: Bao Haus
records.address: 2F, 62-9 Seojeon-ro 38 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47294, South Korea
records.description: When Chef Choi Haeng-rak opened Bao Haus here in his hometown of Busan, his extensive overseas training at last found a place to flourish. His restaurant offers simple and casual Taiwanese-style dishes.

records.name: Cor Pasta bar
records.address: 2F, 13 Dongseong-ro 25 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47305, South Korea
records.description: Walk into a hip alley in Jeonpo-dong, and there is a thick steel door on the second floor of a glass-walled building, behind which is an elegant ten-seater diner. As the name Pasta Bar suggests, this eatery offers a wide selection of its namesake dishes made with fresh housemade pasta.

records.name: Yakitori Onjung
records.address: 9-7 Dongcheon-ro 108 beon-gil, Busanjin-Gu, Busan, 47247, South Korea
records.description: Onjung is a small yakitori bistro run by a couple, who opened their first restaurant here in Busan after acquiring culinary experience in Seoul.

records.name: Good morning Hongkong
records.address: 19 Seojeon-ro 47 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47247, South Korea
records.description: If you pine for Hong Kong cuisine and want to experience a uniquely Hong Kong vibe, this diner deserves your full attention as it is inspired by cha chaan teng, or a Hong Kong-style café. The owner says he opened this joint merely out of his love for Hong Kong.

records.name: L'étang
records.description: L'étang is a French bistro located on one of the main roads in Yeonji-dong. Here, the owner-chef Jung Dong-won does everything single-handedly, from preparing the ingredients to cooking and serving.

records.name: Hapcheon Gukbapjip
records.description: Dwaeji-gukbap (pork and rice soup), the representative culinary delight of Busan, has continued to evolve with changing times and dietary trends. Amid this evolution, the variant served at Hapcheon Gukbapjip has long adhered to the original recipe, delighting customers with its time-tested flavors.

records.name: Niurou mian guan zi
records.address: 25-4 Suyeong-ro 388 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48311, South Korea
records.description: A long line under a yellow awning makes spotting this bustling Taiwanese eatery a breeze. Its streamlined menu features homely yet delectable dishes, including pleasantly spicy Taiwan-style braised beef noodle soup, wonton soup, Taiwanese cold noodles, spicy wonton in chili oil, and tripe in mala sauce.

records.name: Namakzip
records.address: #1068 A, W square, 145 Bunpo-ro, Nam-gu, Busan, 48515, South Korea
records.description: Busan offers a wide variety of dwaeji-gukbap (pork and rice soup), befitting its position as the origin of this dish. Every restaurant adds its own twist to the soup’s broth while staying true to its authentic flavors.

records.name: L'Essence
records.address: 3F, 17 Gwangnam-ro 22 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48307, South Korea
records.description: L'Essence is a French restaurant set in a quiet alley near Namcheon Station. Here, Chef Jeon Ji-seong combines seasonal local ingredients with vibrant sauces to present French cuisine offering an outstanding balance of taste and aroma.

records.name: Anmok
records.address: 3 Gwangnam-ro 22 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48307, South Korea
records.description: Anmok’s unique take on dwaeji-gukbap, or pork and rice soup, may surprise customers with novel flavors and charm that defy their memories of the dish. The soup is not merely unconventional. It’ll make you nod in appreciation.

records.name: Palate
records.description: Palate offers contemporary French cuisine that is free-spirited and adventurous in style. Its sensuous fare is based on the culinary diversity experienced by Chef Kim Jae-hoon.

records.name: Eonyang Bulgogi Busanjip
records.description: More commonly known as just Busanjip, this eatery at Gwangalli Beach has long been a popular spot, always bustling with customers waiting to get in. After decades of business in its previous location, the restaurant moved to this location in 2018.

records.name: Tokyo Babsang
records.description: The familiar vibrant vibe of Gwangalli Beach, a landmark attraction in Busan, will have given way to that of calm and peace by the time one arrives at the door of Tokyo Babsang, which specializes in unaju (grilled eel over rice) and hitsumabushi (Nagoya-style grilled eel), the two representative Japanese eel dishes.

records.name: Vigneto
records.address: 55 Suyeong-ro 522 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48299, South Korea
records.description: Vigneto is the very first restaurant by an owner-chef couple who settled in Busan after studying Italian cuisine at ALMA, the renowned culinary school in Italy. The building is both their home and restaurant, with the wooden ceiling and furniture in the interior creating a cozy and warm vibe.

records.name: Ramsey
records.address: 45 Gwanganhaebyeon-ro 255 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48285, South Korea
records.description: Helmed by Chef Lee Gyu-jin, Ramsey pushes the boundaries of its classic French cuisine through inventive use of ingredients. Located in Millak-dong, the highly competitive dining battleground where eateries of diverse varieties keep popping up, this bistro is set apart from the pack with its alluring French fare.

records.name: Zero Base
records.address: 2F, 17 Millak-ro 33 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48285, South Korea
records.description: Zero Base is a new Japanese restaurant by Chef Yu Byeong-chan, who previously ran the izakaya Yoo No Woo with a stellar reputation. The chef’s unrelenting thirst for classy Japanese cuisine, which had never been fully quenched at his former spot, drove him to present his newly evolved cuisine at this up-and-coming eatery.

records.name: PILI PILI
records.address: 54 Muhak-ro 33 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48268, South Korea
records.description: Take a stroll around Gwangan-dong, and you’ll come across a restaurant whose exterior and interior design will make you ask yourself whether you are in Busan or Thailand. Piri Piri is a Thai-style dining bar that serves Thai cuisine and exotic cocktails.

records.name: Yongkangzzie
records.description: Situated near Gwangalli Beach at the beginning of an alley leading to Millak Golmok Market, Yongkangzzie is a Taiwanese spot best known for its beef noodle soup. The consistent design concepts that permeate both exterior and interior spaces, as well as the detailed décor, have done a remarkable job of reproducing a vibe that evokes Taiwan.

records.name: Yakitori Haegong
records.address: 30-5 Millakbondong-ro 19 beon-gil, Suyoeng-gu, Busan, 48290, South Korea
records.description: In an alley of a quiet residential neighborhood is a pink building with an unexpected tiny little sign that reads “Haegong.” This Japanese eatery specializes in yakitori (grilled chicken skewers) made with native Korean chicken.

records.name: Outro by Vito
records.address: 18 Millakbondong-ro 19 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48087, South Korea
records.description: With the new name Outro by Vito, the restaurant relocated from a location in the Haeridan-gil area to this spot near Gwangalli Beach. Not only did this fine purveyor of natural wine and cuisine change its name, but it also revamped its exterior and décor with a touch of contemporary elegance.

records.name: Delibong
records.address: #110 Noblesse square, 25 Singeum-ro, Yeonje-gu, Busan, 47560, South Korea
records.description: A charcuterie course consisting of housemade meat products – doesn’t that pique your interest? After many years of running a French dining spot, the owner-chef Park Jeong-bong finally opened this little gem with a bar counter and tables that can seat only about ten people.

records.name: Cha Ae Jeon Halmae Kalguksu
records.address: 70 Gwajeong-ro 191 beonga-gil, Yeonje-gu, Busan, 47558, South Korea
records.description: Since 1976, this establishment has faithfully and unwaveringly continued to serve local customers with the simple yet hearty dish of kalguksu (hand-cut noodle soup). Though this humble dish can be found anywhere, the eatery’s variant has distinctive old-fashioned charm derived from its unpretentiousness.

records.name: Le dorer
records.address: 2F, 37 Marine city 3-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48118, South Korea
records.description: Le Dorer’s Marine City location offers a gorgeous seascape. Dorer is a French word that means “to coat with gold.” The restaurant’s name therefore symbolizes its resolve to provide a swanky and beautiful dining experience.

records.name: Iwa
records.address: 2F, 13 Haeundaehaebyeon-ro 209 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48093, South Korea
records.description: The chef, who holds a patent for the aging of fish, prepares aged ingredients with clear intent. Such meticulous preparation, combined with diverse selections, produces stable flavors and gastronomic delights.

records.name: Dim Tao
records.description: Dim sum, a representative Cantonese dish, literally means “touch the heart,” implying that it’s not intended to fill your stomach, but is supposed to be a simple meal.

records.name: Haemok
records.address: 8 Gunam-ro 24 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48094, South Korea
records.description: Popular among both tourists and local regulars, Haemok offers accessible Japanese fare. Its blue fence and inexplicably exotic edifice create a vibe that makes this spot stand out in the neighborhood.

records.name: Nagahama Mangetsu
records.description: Tucked deep within the Haeridan-gil area, this establishment stands out with a long line of diners waiting to be seated. This ramen joint in Busan is the first Korean outpost of a restaurant that started during the 1960s in the Nagahama area in Fukuoka, Japan.

records.name: Buda Myeonoak
records.description: For those familiar with Buda Milmyeon in Banyeo-dong, the name Buda Myeonoak may ring a bell. Relocated to the present location near Haeundae Beach in 2021, this noodle haven offers Pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles made out of 100% buckwheat flour.

records.name: Kumsu Bokguk
records.address: 23 Jungdong 1-ro 43 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48095, South Korea
records.description: Kumsu Bokguk in Haeundae District is the head restaurant of a chain that has many outposts in Seoul and Busan. For more than 50 years since 1970, and across multiple generations, this eatery has delighted seafood lovers as a specialized puffer fish restaurant.

records.name: Shunsai Kubo
records.address: 17 Yangdal-ro 4 beon-gil, Buk-gu, Busan, 46517, South Korea
records.description: Shunsai Kubo is a hitsumabushi (Nagoya-style grilled eel) restaurant helmed by Chef Lee Jae-wook. Trained in Japan, the chef is continually striving to raise the bar on the flavor and quality of his signature dish made only with live Japanese eels (Anguilla japonica).

records.name: Mori
records.address: #2-4, 2F, 24 Haeundaehaebyeon-ro 298 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48099, South Korea
records.description: Co-owned by a Korean chef trained in Japan and his Japanese wife, Mori offers nicely presented authentic Japanese kaiseki dining that will delight both your eyes and palate. Chef Kim Wan-gyu crafts delicate dishes using the fresh seafood and seasonal produce of Busan.

records.name: Sogonggan
records.address: 4F, 47 Haeundaehaebyon-ro 298 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48099, South Korea
records.description: Sogonggan is a double entendre that can be read as “a small space” or “a space dealing with beef.” Its thoughtfully crafted menu is rooted in Korean cuisine. The chef spent many years perfecting his Western cuisine before making the switch to its Korean counterpart.

records.name: Chaoran
records.address: 5F Signiel, 30 Dalmaji-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48099, South Korea
records.description: Situated on the fifth floor of Signiel Busan, Chaoran serves authentic Cantonese cuisine – more precisely its Hong Kong variety, which is based on the former yet characterized by the harmony of new flavors resulting from the city’s culturally diverse geographical contexts.

records.name: Yulling
records.address: 2F, 28 Dalmaji-gil 62 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48098, South Korea
records.description: Yulling sits on the second floor of the Mipo Oceanside Hotel at the beginning of Dalmaji-gil Road. The lengthy counter in this vast space commands a panoramic ocean view marked by the spectacular Dongbaekseom Island and Gwangandaegyo Bridge.

records.name: Torafuguga
records.description: Located on a boulevard near Jungdong Intersection in the Haeundae District, Torafuguga stands out with its quaint wooden exterior and a small aquarium with live torafuku (tiger puffer) at the front. The eatery has no sign except for a small calligraphy of its name penned by the owner-chef Jung Seung-hun himself.

records.name: Fiotto
records.address: Unit H, 2F, Eke, 219, Dalmaji-gil 117beon-gagil, Haeundae-gu, Busan
records.description: Located on Dalmaji Hill, Fiotto is a cozy little bistro run by a couple that serves meals based around pasta dishes. At first, the eatery’s decision to offer a pasta-only course may seem a little odd. But once you experience it, you’ll find the myriad flavors of the varied pasta dishes incredibly enjoyable.

records.name: Mustrue
records.address: 29 Jwadongsunhwan-ro 433 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48114, South Korea
records.description: Mustrue is one of the representative fine dining spots in Busan. Helmed by Chef Jung Jae-yong, a Busan native, it is covertly tucked away in a back alley of Dalmaji-gil Road. Open the golden door, and you’ll be greeted with a bar counter, where the chef masterfully handles everything from cooking to serving.

records.name: 100.1.Pyeongnaeng
records.address: 29 Namcheonbada-ro 10 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48314, South Korea
records.description: 100.1.Pyeongnaeng was a naengmyeon restaurant that ran for exactly 100 days and grabbed the attention of foodies in the latter half of 2023. With a strong passion for cold noodle flavors, Kwak Dong-hoon officially opened the Pyongyang-style naengmyeon restaurant on March 3, 2024. Kwak developed his own Pyongyang naengmyeon recipe after touring naengmyeon restaurants all over Korean in search for the bowl of noodles.

records.name: Bibijae
records.address: 45 Namcheonbada-ro 10 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48314, South Korea
records.description: Bibimbap is a versatile Korean dish with flavors that can drastically change depending on the ingredients. Bibijae offers bibimbap dishes made with creative combinations of ingredients and flavors. Diners can not only enjoy classic bibimbap but also enjoy creative twists with seasonal ingedients.

records.name: Jeongjitgan
records.description: Jeongjitgan is the Gyeongsang-do dialect word for kitchen. Opened in 2011, Jeongjitgan specializes in Busan-style dwejigukbap, or pork soup. The rich, milky broth, which is reminiscent of a clean, savory beef bone broth is prepared fresh daily.

records.name: Hanwolgwan
records.address: 10 Gwangan-ro 62 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48303, South Korea
records.description: A bowl of gomtang at Hanwolgwan is served with generous helpings of their pride in the ingredients and a deep commitment to bring out the best flavors. Hanwolgwan exclusively uses heifer hanwoo beef, which imparts a delicate beef aroma to the broth.

records.name: Born and Bred
records.address: B1F Paradise Hotel, 296 Haeundaehaebyeon-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48099, South Korea
records.description: Premium-grade hanwoo is now served in Busan. Only top-grade female cattle (1++BMS9 grade) are hand-picked daily by highly experienced staff, aged and trimmed to a perfect thickness to create a multi-faceted flavor profile.

records.name: Haeundae Rib Barbecue Restaurant
records.description: A landmark of Busan’s culinary scene, Haeundae Rib barbecue restaurant has stood steadfast since 1964, transitioning from a century-old traditional house to a modernized building while maintaining its rich heritage. Now run by the third generation, this renowned restaurant specializes in just two dishes: fresh ribs and marinated ribs, both exclusively made from cow ribs, as the name suggests.

records.name: Baekgabaekban(백가백반)
records.address: No. 2097, 2F, W Square Shopping Building, 145, Bunpo-ro, Nam-gu
records.menu:
Grilled fish set menu ￦10,900
Seafood ttukbaegi ￦12,000
records.description: It is a Korean-style home-cooked meal restaurant that serves carefully arranged dishes. Grilled fish is popular here, where all the side dishes are made from scratch, and the main dishes are cooked immediately after the orders are placed.

records.name: Miryang Galbi(밀양갈비)
records.description: It is one of the best restaurants in Choryang Pork Ribs Alley and only uses domestic sows. Both seasoned and unseasoned ribs are available, and all the food served is made from scratch.

records.name: Gayapocha Seonjigukbap Main Branch(가야포차선지국밥 본점)
records.menu:
Sugure(beef skin lining) gukbap ￦9,000
Seonji(beef blood curd) gukbap ￦8,000
records.description: This restaurant, which has remained open 24 hours for over 30 years, serves sugure gukbap and other sugure dishes that are hard to findelsewhere. It is a comfortable spot where you can order dishes to go with alcohol after 4 PM.

records.name: Gamasot(30년전통가마솥석쇠돼지갈비)
records.description: This pork ribs specialty restaurant has been operating for over 30 years with a single menu of seasoned domestic pork rib barbecue. All the food is made in-house. The jjigae and praised crab served at each order are delightful beyond expectations.

records.name: DALTHAI (달 타이)
records.menu:
Pu nim pad pong kari ￦33,000
Tom yum goong ￦23,000
records.description: This Thai restaurant has been a fixture on Dalmaji-gil for over a decade. The kitchen is staffed by a team of Thai chefs who use ingredients sourced from Thailand or from contracted local farms.

records.name: RAN A HAN(란아한)
records.description: This place feels like a direct transplant of a shop from the streets of Thailand. Run by a chef with experience in Thai hotels, it offers authentic Thai cuisine with no compromises, staying true to the bold and vibrant flavors of the region.

records.name: BAOHAUS(바오하우스)
records.description: This is a casual restaurant that offers Taiwanese cuisine interpreted in a unique way. You can enjoy Taiwan’s representative dishes, such as bao and beef noodle soup. It is also famous for its fast food service.

records.name: Blue Haven(롯데호텔 부산 블루헤이븐）
records.menu:
Lunch Course ￦65,000-70,000
Dinner Course ￦100,000-150,000
→ Provided as a course menu; the menu may vary depending on the ingredients
records.description: With the comfortable and laid-back atmosphere of a resort by day and the romantic atmosphere of a garden with soft lighting along with the night view of the city by night, Blue Haven offers a casual dining menu and a variety of drinks, including cocktails and wine.

records.name: Monnani Sikdang Haeundae Branch (못난이식당 해운대점)
records.description: This restaurant specializes in cutlassfish dishes using large cutlassfish from Jeju, and you can enjoy fresh tossed cutlassfish. They make healthy food using sweetness from squash.

records.name: Sonnae hyangmi(손내향미)
records.description: Here, guests can watch as their rice is cooked in a stone pot and smell the aroma of Mokpo-style grilled ribs from the hearth that fills the space. After waiting for about 20 minutes, the Mokpo-style galbi sotbap (stone pot rice) is served in an atmosphere where one can focus solely on their meal.

records.name: Seonchang Hoetjip (선창횟집)
records.description: In operation for more than 40 years, Seonchang Hoetjip prepares its own seafood every morning and serves dishes made fresh daily with vegetables delivered that day and handmade kimchi. This is a Korean-style sliced raw fish restaurant that is suitable for a special occasion.

records.name: Elboos by Sooble (엘부스 바이 수블)
records.description: Sooble vows to serve what the chef wants to eat and drink. This popular restaurant-bar offers a view of beautiful scenery and delectable cuisine. The open kitchen, maintained without a spot, makes a great impression.

records.name: Sushi sian (스시시안)
records.description: This sushi restaurant uses red vinegar to prepare shari (vinegared rice), which goes well with fatty fish or blue-backed fish. You can enjoy omakase-level sushi at a relatively affordable price, and the restaurant operates by reservation only.

records.name: JYUGA（쥬가）
records.description: This crowd favorite on Haeridan-gil is run by an owner who trained for many years in kaiseki cuisine in Kyoto, Japan, and his wife, a Japanese chef from Osaka. Together, they make tasty Osaka-based cuisine anyone can enjoy.

records.name: Kuziramen (쿠지라멘)
records.description: When it comes to Japanese ramen, most people think of tonkotsu ramen with a thick broth, but this is a place where you can find shio ramen and shoyu ramen with a clear broth, as well as abura soba. The ramen shop with a dedicated fanbase presents slightly thicker noodles, similar to those used in kalguksu, that have a unique appeal.

records.name: Palate (팔레트)
records.description: A refined dining experience curated by Chef Kim Jae-hoon, where French cooking techniques meet a harmonious blend of diverse ingredients, resulting in creative and sophisticated cuisine.

records.name: 1969 Buwondong Kalguksu Nampo Main Branch (1969부원동칼국수 남포본점)
records.description: To maintain freshness, the restaurant receives the ingredients auctioned off every morning and operates in limited quantities until noodles are sold out. Here, you can enjoy noodles topped with plenty of fresh oysters and scallops. Typically, the ingredients are exhausted around 6 PM.

records.name: Mackerel Research Institute Main Branch(고등어연구소 본점)
records.menu:
Stone pot rice with mackerel with ochazuke ￦10,900
Warm soba with mackerel ￦10,900
records.description:
This restaurant perfected the art of serving
mackerel dishes in the freshest way possible through various research. It offers a wide array of Japanese-cuisine-based dishes, including stone pot rice with mackerel, warm soba with mackerel, and mackerel sushi.

records.name: DONGSAMJUNG (동삼정)
records.description: This is a Korean bar where you can enjoy unique Korean fusion dishes made with Western cooking methods in a clean space. It serves seasonal dishes that go well with various types of alcoholic drinks.

records.name: Yuwon(유원)
records.menu:
Five-spice braised pork ￦38,000
Chili shrimp ￦35,000
Guangdong noodles ￦11,000
records.description: Located a little away from the downtown area near the Komodo Hotel, it doesn’t seem to have any outstanding features at first glance, but it is a Chinese restaurant where the owner-chef, who is of Chinese descent and has been in charge of the kitchen for more than 50 years, cooks the food himself.

records.name: Yasumaru Ninniku
records.description: The restaurant started out to present good food when people lose their appetite in the summer. But it’s known for the long queue regardless of the season. It’s known for parang guksu noodles with a unique appearance and not having a signboard.

records.name: Jeez (지즈)
records.menu:
Sirloin katsu set meal ￦13,000
Tenderloin katsu set meal ￦14,000
records.description: This restaurant, located in a small alley, serves Japanese-style tonkatsu with Western elements. As the name of the restaurant, Jeez(short for Jesus), suggests, it aims to serve food that will impress you the first time you taste it.

records.name: Shunsai Kubo Hwamyeong Branch (슌사이쿠보 화명)
records.description: Shunsai Kubo is a restaurant specializing in hitsumabushi, a Nagoya-style eel rice bowl that uses only the finest Pungcheon eels. It offers traditionally prepared eel, grilled with care by brushing special sauce, as well as dishes for children to enjoy.

records.name: DELI BONG (델리봉)
records.description: DELI BONG, run by a single-owner chef, offers French course dining using charcuterie. Upon the first visit, guests may be a little confused because there is no signboard, but there is definitely a feast going on inside.

records.name: Bonheur Pâtisserie (보느파티쓰리)
records.description: This is a French dessert shop run by pastry chef Kim Ji-yeon, who graduated from Le Cordon Bleu in France and worked at Hotel Shangri-La Paris and Hotel Ritz Paris for 14 years.

records.name: Namcheonmeonga (남천면가)
records.menu:
Perilla oil buckwheat noodles ￦11,000
Namcheon soba ￦12,000
records.description: This restaurant serves buckwheat noodles that are made from scratch daily from domestic buckwheat. They put a lot of effort and time into each bowl of food to serve healthy food to customers.

records.name: Dakbaljizon(닭발의 지존)
records.description: This is a restaurant with a heritage that has been only serving chicken feet and clam soup for over 40 years. The spicy seasoning of the chicken feet made from scratch goes fantastically well with the nourishing broth of the clam soup. It has been beloved by many people in the area for a long time.

records.name: Daily Lucky (데일리럭키)
records.menu:
Italian ham and cheese sandwich ￦9,200
Carottes Râpées Sandwich ￦8,700
records.description: This cozy and pleasant bakery opens every morning at 7:00 with sourdough bread, sandwiches, and hot soup. The sourdough bread is made of organic domestic wheat.

records.name: 100.1.pyeongnaeng (백일평냉)
records.description: With the traditional flavors and the principle of the cold noodle technicians, the restaurant has completed the art of making authentic Pyeongyang naengmyeon, consisting of beef broth, salt, and 80% buckwheat noodles. The menu also includes homemade North Korean manduguk (dumpling soup) and Hanwoo bulgogi.

records.name: Afekt (아펙트)
records.menu:
Squid ceviche ￦28,000
Spinach shrimp oil sauce tajarin ￦25,000
records.description: This impressive restaurant with a large U-shaped table is a French-based dining restaurant that uses seasonal ingredients and offers a menu that pairs great with wine.

records.name: Yakitori BAEKTAN Gwangalli (야키토리 백탄 광안리)
records.description: All the skewers are served on the same day as they are made using chicken that has been deboned by hand every morning. This yakitori specialty restaurant follows the principle of serving what is cooked on the same day. To order, choose a course first, then add individual items. You can enjoy well-grilled skewers in various ways.

records.name: Yakitori HAEGONG (야키토리 해공)
records.description: This place, which has an atmosphere like that of a high-end Japanese restaurant, serves yakitori, which is made by boning and carefully grilling Korean native chickens. It is also a unique place where kkomjangeo (hagfish), which are caught on the same day and grilled over charcoal, are also popular.

records.name: Wooripocha Main Branch (우리포차 본점)
records.description: This restaurant, which serves yellowtail sashimi(sliced raw fish) made with only wild yellowtail weighing 10 kg or more caught in Gangwon-do and Jeju-do, is always full of customers from the moment it opens. Must-order items include grilled yellowtail heads and yellowtail sashimi.

records.name: EUTTEUM Iroribata (으뜸이로리바타)
records.description: The fish being grilled in the Japanese-style hearth “irori” adds an exotic atmosphere to this restaurant, which serves a variety of Japanese course meals centered on charcoal-grilled dishes using the hearth. It operates on a reservation basis.

records.name: Jamae Gukbap (자매국밥)
records.menu:
Steamed pork slices ￦10,000
Dwaeji gukbap(pork soup with rice) ￦10,000
records.description: This is a hole-in-the-wall that has been loved by the locals for over 30 years, serving broth made from fresh pork head meat every day. The soup is rich and strong, flavored with doenjang-based seasoning.

records.name: Joyful joyful (조이풀조이풀)
records.description: The Japanese-style bar, which can seat about 10 people, serves seasonal fish dishes and Japanese-style street Chinese food that are hard to find in Korea. It is a good pub where both the atmosphere and the food are enjoyable.

records.name: Cheongsan1954(청산1954)
records.menu:
Pork belly bossam with small octopus in cypress steamer(1 person) ￦23,000
Stir-fried octopus(1 person) ￦14,500
records.description: This restaurant serves a pork belly dish first boiled with 12 Korean medicinal herbs and steamed in cypress wood, along with a side of fresh leafy greens grown in a hydroponic system for 576 hours. The space was created by renovating a wooden building established in 1968.

records.name: Haeundae Rib Barbecue Restaurant (해운대암소갈비집)
records.menu:
Fresh beef ribs ￦63,000
Spicy beef ribs ￦59,000
records.description: Established in 1964, this family-owned beef rib barbecue restaurant has been in business for two generations. It is a widely known establishment for its traditional Hanok-style architecture and signature marinade.

records.name: Yeonhwa bakery
records.menu:
Cake(price may vary) Seasonal flavors
Baked goods(price may vary) Monthly flavors
records.description: At Yeonhwa Bakery, you can find desserts made with healthy and wholesome ingredients in a quiet and clean space. They make cakes and baked goods using seasonal fruits and vegetables.

records.name: Daeseong Galchi Jjigaegui (대성갈치찌개구이)
records.menu:
Galchi Jjigae(cutlassfish stew) for 1 ￦43,000
Galchi Gui(grilled cutlassfish) for 1 ￦43,000
records.description: A Daebyeon Port restaurant with many local regulars that serves stewed and grilled galchi (cutlassfish), anchovy sliced raw fish, and jjigae (stew). The dishes are made of fresh raw anchovies and raw cutlass fish from Jeju Island, with chunky volume and tender flavor.

records.name: GOGIHYUNG (고기형)
records.description: At this premium Korean beef restaurant, the owner, who is serious about meat, carefully ages selected Hanwoo beef and makes daily recommendations for guests. They offer Hanwoo tongue and fresh fatty brisket, which are hard to come by.

records.name: Woobong Shabu
records.menu:
Korean beef brisket shabu shabu
(1 person) ￦19,000
Set for 2 ￦58,000
records.description: This premium shabu shabu is made with only the finest 1++-rated beef and is cooked in a paper pot. Everything in sight, including the food served, is neat and carefully organized.

records.name: Hytte roastery Jeonpo Branch (히떼로스터리 전포점)
records.description: Both the space and the coffee are meant to be relaxing and smooth to the last drop, and it puts the most time and effort into making sure the coffee is balanced and has a clean aftertaste.

records.name: Le dorer
records.address: 2F, 37 Marine city 3-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48118, South Korea
records.description: Le Dorer’s Marine City location offers a gorgeous seascape. Dorer is a French word that means “to coat with gold.” The restaurant’s name therefore symbolizes its resolve to provide a swanky and beautiful dining experience.

records.name: Songheonjip
records.address: 18 Millak-ro 19 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48285, South Korea
records.description:
With successful businesses built around traditional liquor and noodle soup, the owner-chef now ventures into tteokgalbi at Songheonjip.
Thick, charcoal-grilled patties are smoky and juicy, served with rice, delicate banchan, and a rich doenjang jjigae. Set in a renovated two-storey house, the restaurant evokes the cosy atmosphere of a 1990s home. Dishes are served on low tables for a homey yet hearty dining experience. Shoe-off required when entering the room.

records.name: Moemiljip
records.address: 2F, Orange Plaza, 23 Marine city 3-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48118, South Korea
records.description:
Using 100% Korean buckwheat and milling the noodles in-house, this restaurant invites you to appreciate the pure flavour and chewy texture of freshly made buckwheat noodles. While the bibim buckwheat noodles focus on a spicy bite, the perilla-oil and cold buckwheat noodles showcase the delicate aroma of buckwheat that the restaurant aims to highlight.
The bouncy, tender slices of boiled pork also pair well with the noodles.

records.name: Pyeongyangjip
records.description:
Pyeongyangjip serves North Korean-style mandu and nokdujeon. The house-made dumplings, filled with kimchi, glass noodles, tofu, and vegetables, are encased in silky wrappers and served with a clear broth of beef brisket and shank.
The nokdujeon, made from mung beans finely milled on a stone metdol, is airy and crispy, accented by crunchy bean sprouts. Prepared by the owner and family in this intimate, spotless space, the mandu-guk here is sure to warm the heart.

records.name: 1969 Buwondong Kalguksu
records.address: 3 Gudeok-ro 22 beon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan, 48954, South Korea
records.description:
After several relocations, the restaurant continues to serve diners the same traditional flavours. The menu is extremely simple yet highly focused, offering only kalguksu and mandu.
The kalguksu is a must-try: house-made noodles with a firm, chewy texture paired with a clear, deeply savoury broth. For spicy lovers, the bibim kalguksu captures distinctly bold and tangy Busan-style flavours. A larger portion can be requested at no extra cost.

records.name: Matsuzaki
records.description:
This intimate restaurant offers authentic kaiseki omakase by the chef who trained at a renowned culinary institute. The petite yet cosy space is decorated with fine tableware and glassware, along with paintings by the chef’s mother.
The meal opens with a flavourful soup, followed by a beautifully composed hassun of seasonal bites, and concludes with a nabemono of freshly cooked rice, vegetables, and fish—Japanese cuisine that remains faithful to its fundamentals.

records.name: Meerok Super
records.description:
Meerok Super is a small six-seat restaurant that serves outsize creativity. The vegetables grown in the on-site vegetable patch, aged fish and meat, and seasonal ingredients are transformed into the day’s tasting menu.
The grilled meat course, cooked over charcoal for aroma, texture, and juiciness, and served with rice, creates a seamless transition from Western to Korean flavours. Expect to be delighted by unexpected yet harmonious flavour combinations that change daily.

records.name: Unaju
records.description:
Perched on a quiet hillside in Cheongsapo, Unaju features a sleek black exterior. It brings to Korea the recipes of Shirakawa, a restaurant founded in Nagoya in 1948. The eel is grilled twice to enhance the springy and crispy texture. Served with a special tare sauce, it pairs perfectly with rice.
For a different experience, try it as ochazuke by adding wasabi, green tea, and shredded gim. The lunch special includes sides of cold udon and tempura. Do plan ahead as only 30 portions are available by reservation each day.

records.name: Ultra bite
records.description:
With its sleek, modern façade, Ultra bite stands at the end of a small Gwanganri alley. Run by young chefs trained in Australia and Seoul, the restaurant offers refined, imaginative yet approachable dishes and wines.
Highlights include whole grilled squid served with anchovy cream, lardo, and fermented tomato pickles, as well as deep-fried whole king oyster mushrooms coated in a sweet and spicy ginger sauce. The lime juice and seaweed flakes served on the side add a distinctive twist to the dish.

records.name: IAán
records.description:
This restaurant showcases bold contemporary flavours derived from classic French and Korean cuisine. The dish names are Korean, yet the sauces and plating are distinctly French.
The chef's remarkable ability to balance sauces suggests even more promising work to come. Cosy carpets and minimalist tables create an atmosphere that is warm, calm, and refined, much like the food. This is a lovely, quiet place to unwind over good food and wine.

records.name: Zandunga
records.address: 41 Dongcheon-ro 108 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47247, South Korea
records.description:
Tucked away in a quiet alley, this spot combines an industrial, chic interior with lively music for a relaxed, inviting atmosphere. Inspired by his passion for Mexican cuisine, the chef started this restaurant.
Everything from tortillas to fillings and sauces is made in-house. Fresh tortillas are prepared every morning, with colourful variations crafted from different corn varieties. The pork taco is a must-try. Warm, attentive service completes the dining experience.

records.name: Jin Dweji Gomtang
records.address: 2F, 4 Gwanganhaebyeon-ro 284 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48283, South Korea
records.description:
Since opening in 2024, this spot has quickly become a favourite among Busan’s younger crowd. Its charming space centres on a U-shaped counter, creating an atmosphere that feels both lively and intimate.
The signature dweji gomtang is made with Berkshire K black pork from the Jirisan region, prized for producing a clean, delicate broth. Another highlight is the suyuk nengchae, featuring precisely sliced pork belly with tender lean meat and fat that melts in the mouth, leaving a satisfying finish.

records.name: Tooru
records.address: Unit 203, Kyungdong Leen View 2nd Apartment, 1 Gunam-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48095, South Korea
records.description:
The chef crafts the omakase around daily-sourced seafood, highlighting a spectrum of nuanced flavours. Staying true to the seasonality central to Japanese cuisine, he incorporates Korean ingredients at their peak. Local seafood takes centre stage in dishes rooted in simple, authentic recipes.
Among the chef’s signatures are somen dishes, served either in the surinagashi style or with sauces made from seasonal ingredients. Despite its compact size, the bar-centred layout creates a comfortable, relaxed atmosphere.

records.name: Pyeongsanok
records.description:
yeongsanok, a family-run restaurant with over a century of history, continues to be celebrated for its steadfast dedication to tradition. It possesses the charm of a neighbourhood eatery with a nostalgic warmth.
The menu is simple—suyuk and noodles, with yeolmu noodles as a summer addition. The suyuk, made from carefully selected Korean pork with a balanced fat-to-lean ratio, is slowly simmered to achieve a tender texture and clean, delicate flavour.

records.name: Shabuniji (샤브니지)
records.description: A nearly century-old Japanese colonial-era house has been reinterpreted as a refined space reminiscent of a traditional Japanese ryokan. The restaurant offers a variety of broths and Korean beef graded 1++, allowing guests to enjoy a distinctive meal alongside beautiful landscaping.

records.name: Digeut (디귿)
records.menu:
Yakitori Course ￦29,000
Top 5 Yakitori Osusume (Chef’s Selection) ￦16,000
records.description: Fresh chicken delivered each dawn from a poultry facility is carefully trimmed and grilled over premium binchotan charcoal. Despite specializing in yakitori, the restaurant is surprisingly popular with an older clientele. The name itself, taken from the Korean consonant “ㄷ,” the initial sound of dak (chicken), reflects the restaurant’s sincere dedication to yakitori.

records.name: Italy Samchon (이태리 삼촌)
records.description: Thick cuts of meat are fried to a crisp and served with house-made tonkatsu sauce. In a cozy setting, the restaurant takes pride in preparing tonkatsu that is always moist and tender, made with genuine care.

records.name: Gijang Beach Straw-Fire Grilled Hagfish (기장해변짚불곰장어)
records.description: This restaurant grills fresh hagfish, delivered daily, over straw fire so that diners can fully experience its natural freshness and flavor. The hagfish can also be enjoyed with seasoning, and a variety of side dishes prepared directly by the owner are served together. The young radish mulgimchi is especially memorable for its distinctive taste.

records.name: Restaurant Ambience (레스토랑 엠비언스)
records.menu:
Lunch ￦88,000
Dinner ￦149,000
(Prices may vary depending on the season)
records.description: This contemporary Korean dining restaurant carefully brings out refined flavors using fresh local ingredients such as kelp and seaweed. The space, which harmonizes beautifully with the landscape of Gijang, was completed after two years of discussion and planning.

records.name: Mansedam (만세담)
records.menu:
Someorigomtang (Beef Head Meat Soup) ￦11,000
Oribaeksuk (Whole Duck Soup) ￦76,000
records.description: This restaurant is run by Korean cuisine master chef Park Gyeong-rye, who has received numerous awards. Many people visit to enjoy the gomtang that the master chef personally prepares in a traditional cauldron. The side dishes served with the meal are also made with seasonal vegetables that are grown and harvested by the chef.

records.name: Ilgwang Bada Hoetjip (일광바다횟집)
records.menu:
Myeolchissambap (Leaf Wraps and Rice with Anchovies) ￦15,000
Daegutang (Codfish Soup) ￦20,000
records.description: This restaurant prepares its dishes using fresh seasonal seafood sourced from Hakri Port, the largest fishing port in Ilgwang-eup. In addition to its well-known anchovy ssambap, the restaurant also offers a variety of popular seasonal dishes.

records.name: Miso Oden (미소오뎅)
records.menu:
Sujiodentang (Oden with Beef Tendons) ￦27,000-32,000
Suji (Beef Tendons) ￦18,000
records.description: When evening falls, this place is always filled with people. The warm and nostalgic atmosphere of the oden bar makes it easy to strike up conversations even with strangers sitting nearby.

records.name: Jungjaejip (정재집)
records.menu:
Mushroom Cream Bacon Gnocchi ￦18,000
Di Napoli e Rucola ￦17,000
records.description: This Italian restaurant, known for its gnocchi, feels like a bistro tucked away on a quiet European alley. The cozy interior is clean and well maintained, and the restaurant offers friendly service along with delicious food.

records.name: Oseongjip (오성집)
records.menu:
Jeju Fresh Pork Belly (130g) ￦13,000
Jeju Fresh Five-Layer Pork Belly (130g) ￦12,500
records.description: At this grill restaurant, thick cuts of meat are skillfully cooked by the staff at the table. The restaurant is known for using juicy, fresh pork from Jeju, and the spicy braised bean sprouts served alongside enhance the flavor of the meat.

records.name: Gwihwasikdang Sakeui Hyang (귀화식당 사케의향)
records.description: This restaurant offers a welcome combination of aged sashimi in various selections, delicate dishes reminiscent of fine dining, and an extensive sake list. Guests can enjoy authentic Japanese flavors here, including the house specialty omurice, which has become something of a signature dish.

records.name: Dangmiok Hanwoo Gomtang Oncheon Main Branch (당미옥 한우곰탕 온천본점)
records.menu:
Premium Hanwoo Gomtang (Beef Bone Soup) ￦8,800
Hanwoo Doganitang (Korean Beef Tendon Soup) ￦16,000
records.description: Founded in 1986 and now run by the second generation, this restaurant carefully selects high-quality cattle directly through the auction process and works closely with its own meat processing facilities. Guests can enjoy gomtang filled generously with beef, served in a rich broth that has been slowly simmered over time.

records.name: Sukjung Galbi (석정갈비)
records.description: This restaurant is run by a livestock product specialist who studied animal science. The meat is prepared through 300 hours of low-temperature aging, cut to an optimal thickness of 15 mm, and scored with precise 4 mm intervals. The restaurant also serves house-made side dishes prepared with vegetables grown by the owner’s parents.

records.name: Jumunjin Makguksu (주문진막국수)
records.description: It’s a very famous restaurant near the Sajik Baseball Stadium, the holy ground of professional baseball. In summer, you have to wait a long time before enjoying their food. This restaurant is a top makguksu specialty shop in Busan. It’s also known for the extremely tender steamed pork.

records.name: Kurumi Sweets (쿠루미 과자점)
records.description: This bakery makes bread using a variety of natural starters cultivated in-house and blends several types of flour that are not easily found. It is a must-visit destination for anyone planning a bakery tour in Busan.

records.name: Kappo Hyeon (갓포현)
records.description: Run by Chef Hyeon Yeong-gil, this restaurant serves authentic Japanese kappo cuisine using the finest seasonal ingredients. Guests can enjoy refined course meals and à la carte dishes shaped by the chef’s many years of experience. It has long been a beloved dining spot in Seomyeon.

records.name: Gaetmaeul Hoetjip (갯마을횟집)
records.menu:
Wild Flounder (Small, for 2) ￦80,000
Black Seabream (Small, for 2) ￦65,000
records.description: This restaurant serves only two kinds of sashimi: wild-caught flounder in spring and summer, and black seabream in autumn and winter. The fish, sourced directly every two days, is served simply but generously. Opened in 1976, the restaurant has been run by two generations.

records.name: Yaki chori (야키쵸리)
records.description: Watching the skewers grilling over charcoal at the counter creates the feeling of being in a local Japanese izakaya. This small skewer grill restaurant tucked away in an alley of Jeonpo-dong offers a variety of yakitori made with fresh chicken.

records.name: Yakitori Onjeong (야키토리 온정)
records.menu:
Tojongdak (Native Korean Chicken) Yakitori Omakase ￦33,000
Mini Course ￦19,000
records.description: Here, locally raised native chicken, carefully prepared each morning, is grilled one skewer at a time over the fire and served in an omakase-style course. Each skewer is cooked to bring out the most appealing flavor of every part of the chicken.

records.name: Yongkangjie Seomyeon Branch (융캉찌에 서면점)
records.description: Named after Yongkang Street, a famous street in Taiwan, this restaurant specializes in Taiwanese cuisine. With an atmosphere that captures the vibes of Taiwan, the restaurant serves rich beef noodle soup and spicy dandan noodles prepared to suit Korean tastes.

records.name: Narutteo Guksu (나룻터국수)
records.description: This restaurant prepares its broth using high-quality dried fish such as sardines and anchovies, and welcomes guests with house-made kkakdugi and kimchi. Its handmade sujebi, torn by hand in the traditional style and known for its pleasantly chewy texture, is especially popular.

records.name: L’Essence (레썽스)
records.menu:
Dinner Tasting Course ￦180,000
Lunch Tasting Course ￦80,000
records.description: This innovative French restaurant uses housemade natural vinegar, soy sauce, and doenjang throughout its menu. The cuisine combines classic French techniques with Korean seasonal ingredients, along with traditional fermentation and pickling methods. Guests can also enjoy watching the cooking process through the open kitchen.

records.name: Brunch Restaurant Sobo (브런치식당 소보)
records.menu:
Sobo Brunch ￦15,000
Beef and Truffle Cream Sandwich ￦16,500
records.description: This restaurant prepares warm and comforting dishes by roasting, steaming, and boiling at least fifteen kinds of fresh seasonal vegetables. The vegetables used are reliable seasonal produce harvested directly by the owner’s parents in the countryside.

records.name: Anmok (안목)
records.menu:
Dwaejigukbap (Pork and Rice Soup) ￦10,000
Samgyeopsuyuk (Steamed Pork Belly) ￦16,000
records.description: With its bar-style seating centered around an open kitchen, the interior may remind visitors of a Japanese ramen shop. However, this restaurant is clearly a dwaejigukbap spot that reinterprets Busan’s iconic dish with a modern sensibility.

records.name: Seogawon Guksu (서가원 국수)
records.menu:
Kongguksu (Noodles in Cold Soybean Soup) ￦9,000
Janchiguksu (Banquet Noodles) ￦6,500
records.description: The soybeans used for the restaurant’s kongguksu are Jangdan beans from Paju, soaked the day before and seasoned simply with water and sun-dried sea salt from Sinan. The result is a soybean broth that is creamy, mild, and deeply nutty. Janchiguksu made with broth prepared from anchovies from Namhae is also popular.

records.name: Chef Gon (쉐프곤)
records.menu:
Grilled Shrimp with Bisque Sauce ￦17,000
Grilled Octopus with Pumpkin Sauce ￦32,000-52,000
records.description: Every morning, a chef with many years of experience in hotel restaurants prepares seasonal menus using fresh ingredients sourced daily. The confidently prepared “Jagalchi Chef Course Special” will give you a whole new experience of Jagalchi Market.

records.name: Geodae Gomtang (거대곰탕)
records.menu:
Gogi Gomtang (Clear Broth/Milky Broth) ￦19,000
Hanwoo Suyuk (Boiled Korean Beef Slices) ￦67,000 / 87,000
records.description: This restaurant slowly simmers carefully selected Korean beef bones using traditional methods to produce a rich and smooth broth. It offers a variety of styles of gomtang and aims to present Korean soup cuisine that can be appreciated on a global stage.

records.name: DAUPHINE (도핀느)
records.description: Having worked at a charcuterie shop in Paris and earned professional certification there, the chef brings that experience to this French charcuterie specialty shop, where all products are made in-house. The restaurant focuses on charcuterie-style dishes that can also be enjoyed as a full meal.

records.name: MUSBI (무스비)
records.description: This restaurant presents a variety of soba dishes with a modern touch and makes its Japanese-style buckwheat noodles in-house. Popular menu items include simmered herring soba and grilled mackerel soba, known for their clean and rich flavors without any fishy taste. Side dishes such as shrimp tempura and tamagoyaki are also available.

records.name: Shindo Lab 2.0 (신도랩 2.0)
records.menu:
Hanwoo No. 9 Porterhouse ￦300,000-400,000
Hanwoo No. 9 Rib Eye ￦200,000-300,000
records.description: Renovated from Shindo Livestock Distribution, the ninth butcher shop established in Busan in 1975, this space carries on its legacy as the second location of Shindo Market’s Shindo Lab. While the first location, Shindo Lab 1.0, offers a course-style dining experience, Shindo Lab 2.0 operates as a steak and oyster bar.

records.name: Yangsan Gukbap (양산국밥)
records.menu:
Toryeom Dwaeji Gukbap (Pork Soup with Rice) ￦12,000
Milmyeon (Cold Wheat Noodles) ￦11,000
records.description: This restaurant has been run by three generations in Haeundae and serves Busan-style clear dwaejigukbap (pork soup with rice). Its clear broth is served at an ideal temperature for toryeom, the traditional method of briefly soaking rice in hot broth. Notably, the restaurant uses brassware bowls that enhance the advantages of the toryeom style.

records.name: Ogi Boribap (옥이보리밥)
records.menu:
Boribap Jeongsik (Barley Rice Set) ￦11,000
Haemulpajeon (Seafood and Green Onion Pancake) ￦17,000
records.description: This restaurant prepares a hearty barley rice set each morning with ten carefully prepared seasonal vegetables and side dishes. Here, the kitchen remains committed to serving an honest and comforting meal every day.

records.name: Yulling (율링)
records.menu:
Special Lunch Course ￦120,000
Special Dinner Course ￦215,000
records.description: This contemporary dining restaurant is run by Chef Kim Seong-ju, formerly of Tokyo’s Michelin three-star restaurant Sézanne and the one-star restaurant L’Amant Secret in Seoul, together with Sommelier Park Min-uk, a winner of a national sommelier competition in Korea and a representative at the Asian Sommelier Competition.

records.name: Fiotto (피오또)
records.description: This farm-to-table restaurant is run by a husband-and-wife chef team who create their courses using ingredients they grow themselves together with their parents. All vegetables used are harvested directly from their farm, while other ingredients are sourced locally. With a focus on regional produce, the restaurant aims to create good food using high-quality ingredients.

records.name: Jyugajunghyo (쥬가정효)
records.description: The owner, who trained in kaiseki cuisine for many years in Kyoto, prepares carefully curated course meals using seasonal ingredients. The courses are designed to pair especially well with Japanese sake.

records.name: マンドゥリ ゴンドゥレパブ (만드리곤드레밥)
records.address: 江西区コンハンアプギル85番ギル13
records.menu: 石焼きゴンドゥレ定食, かぼちゃと鴨の燻製
records.description:
ゴンドゥレパブには一般的に乾燥させたコンドゥレナムルが使われるが、このお店では生のゴ
ンドゥレナムルを使って釜飯を作る。テンジャンチゲとともに10種類以上のおかずが並ぶ石焼
きゴンドゥレ定食が人気。

records.name: ミンムルガーデン (민물가든)
records.address: 釜山広域市江西区屯致中央ギル5
records.menu: 古漬けとフナ煮物, フナ蒸し
records.description: 開業30年の魚の蒸し料理専門店で、伝統的な木の蒸籠で蒸すのが特徴。20種類 以上の材料を混ぜてつくるたれを使用し、白菜キムチの古漬けを用いたフナの煮 物やフナの蒸し物が代表メニュー。

records.name: カヤハルメミル麺
records.address: 釜山広域市蓮堤区ワールドカップ通り145番ギル32
records.menu: 水ミル麺, 拌荞麦面(ビビンミル麺)
records.description: 釜山の郷土料理であるミル麺専門店で、小麦粉にコーンスターチを混ぜて いるため他のミル麺専門店よりも弾力性のある麺が特徴的。スープは豚骨 と牛骨以外にも様々な野菜や複数の韓薬材を混ぜて作り、サイドメニュー の餃子も人気だ。

records.name: 国際ミル麺本店 (국제밀면 본점)
records.address: 蓮堤区中央大路1235番ギル23-6
records.menu:
水ミル麺 ￦9,000
ビビンミル麺 ￦9,000
records.description:
小麦麺(ミルミョン)専門店の中でも特に美味しいと有名なこのお店は
牛骨だけを使ったスープなど独創的な小麦麺を作っている。
通常、機械で切られた薄切りゆで肉がゴミョン(盛り付け)としてのせられるが、このお店では一つ一つ
手で薄く裂いた肩バラ肉がのせられるのが特徴。

records.name: ガヤミルミョン(伽耶小麦麺) (가야밀면)
records.menu: ミル麺, ビビンミル麺
records.description:
さっぱりした味のスープが印象的な40年の伝統を誇るミルミョン(小麦麺)専門店で、
食事時には常に長い列ができるが、140席が確保された広い店舗なので 
待ち時間は短いほう。いつも清潔に管理されている清々しいお店。

records.name: タリン コイントン ダック
records.address: 中区 中区路 47番キル 34
records.description:
3代にわたって約60年営む有名店。メニューは
唯一フライドチキンのみで、一番おいしいチキン
といえばいつも話にあがるお店。

records.name: 釜山コムジャンオ店  ソンイルチプ
records.menu: コムジャンオ塩焼き, コムジャンオヤンニョム焼き
records.description:
1950年から3代にわたって74年間営む、最も有
名なウナギ専門店の一つ。生きている新鮮な国
内産ヌタウナギと23種類の韓方薬を使った特別
な調味料を使用し調理する。

records.name: ベビジャンポッサム久瑞店 (배비장보쌈)
records.menu: ベビジャンポッサム, 盛り合わせポッサム
records.description:
30年以上営む釜山で有名なポサム店の一つで、
自家製のポサムキムチとムチェを毎日漬けている。
おかずとして出される茶碗蒸しも人気で、お客様をもてなす時に重宝するお店。

records.name: ジャンスジャンコリコムタン (장수장꼬리곰탕)
records.menu: 牛テールコムタン, 韓牛の膝蓋骨スープ
records.description:
1983年に開業し40年以上営んでいる。キムチと塩辛は手作りした後に壺で 
熟成させる。骨と膝蓋骨は韓牛、牛テールはオーストラリア産で厳選された材料を使用し、
いつも変わらない味で人気がある。

records.name: 錦繍ポックク本店 (금수복국 해운대본점)
records.address: 釜山広域市海雲台区中洞1路43番ギル23
records.menu:
シロサバフグスープ (スープ / 辛いスープ) ￦15,000 / 16,000
サバフグスープ (スープ / 辛いスープ) ￦22,000 / 23,000
records.description:
ふぐスープ(ポックク)の元祖といえる50年続く伝
統のふぐ料理店。新鮮な原材料と正確な物流シ
ステム、醤類はすべて自家製を使うのが味の秘
訣だという。24時間営業している。

records.name: タオン (다온)
records.address: 釜山広域市海雲台区海雲台海辺路154
records.menu: タオン食卓、ソンアリ食卓
records.description: 韓屋の伝統的なモチーフを活用したインテリアが印象的な韓国料理専門店。郷 土色豊かな小物で飾られた部屋もあり、各種の集まりや格式のある集まりにもよ く利用されている。漢方薬材と旬の食材を使用した韓定食が人気。

records.name: ハルメチェチョプクク (할매재첩국)
records.address: 沙上区 洛東通り1530番ギル20-15
records.menu:
チェチョプクク ￦8,000
シジミの刺身 ￦10,000
records.description:
洛東江辺にあるシジミ料理グルメタウンで30年以上営んでいるシジミスープ専門店で、
ビビン器に一緒に出てくる味噌とシジミを入れ
ビビンバを作ってシジミスープと一緒に食べるのが人気。

records.name: イェイジェ (예이제)
records.address: 釜山広域市海雲台区海雲台海辺路298番ギル29、2階
records.description: 海雲台ビーチの近くにある韓定食専門店で、家族の集まりや接待などに適して いる。店主自らが選んだ旬の食材や知人の経営する農場で採れた野菜を使用 しており、食べるのがもったいないくらい盛り付けにも気を配っている。

records.name: 陜川一流テジクッパ (합천일류돼지국밥)
records.menu: コギクッパ, スユク白飯
records.description:
おいしい店が多いことで知られる沙上(ササン)市外バスターミナルの近くでも特に有名な豚クッパ「テ
ジクッパ」の専門店。24時間営業のため観光客が多く訪れる場所でもある。ニンニクとタデギ(辛味噌)
が山盛りに乗せられているのが特徴であり、クッパのみならず茹で豚肉「スユク」も有名だ。

records.name: 元祖ソッテチュオタン (원조석대추어탕)
records.address: 釜山広域市海雲台区盤松路571番ギル5
records.menu: チュオタン, エイ蒸し
records.description: 入口を入ると、高く積み上げられ薪とかまどの上の鋳鉄釜が目に入ってくる、有名 なチュオタン(どじょう鍋)専門店。強力な火で長時間煮るので柔らかく豊かな味わ いが楽しめる。ノンゴドン(たにし)の和え物とホンオチム(エイの蒸し物)も人気。

records.name: ハルメボクグク (할매복국)
records.menu: ふぐちり, シロサバフグのゆで肉
records.description: 「ふぐ村」として知られているミポ(尾浦)地域の代表的なふぐ料理専門店。 釜山の郷土料理店38か所のうちの一つ。ふぐちりが代表メニューで、 ほかにもふぐのお粥とスユク、焼き物、蒸し物などの料理も味わえる。

records.name: シンチャンクッパ (신창국밥)
records.description:
1969年に国際市場の新昌洞(シンチャンドン)で始まり、シンチャンクッパと名付けられた有名店で、
澄んだスープのテジクッパの始まりとされる。
新鮮な材料や伝統的な方法であるトゥェヨム(退染)にこだわり、自家製の北部式スンデも人気がある。

records.name: 平安道豚足  (평안도족발)
records.address: 釜山広域市海雲台区タルマジキル14
records.description: 30年以上、この場所で営んできた伝統ある豚足専門店。地元の人にも長く愛され てきた店らしく、豚足特有の臭さがない、バランスのとれた美味しさが特徴。 冷菜豚足とニンニク豚足などのメニューも人気。

records.name: 韓牛炭火ヤンゴプチャン (한우숯불양곱창)
records.address: 釜山広域市海雲台区海雲台海辺路385
records.description: 海雲台中洞駅近くのヤンゴプチャン専門店で、特に牛の第一胃袋である特羊味 付け焼きが有名である。注文と同時に特製タレを塗り、店員が焼いてくれる特羊 焼きはとてもやわらかいながらも軽く弾力のある食感が特徴である。

records.name: サンドゥンイテジ クッパ
records.menu:
テジクッパ ￦10,000
スユク(ゆで肉) ￦12,000
records.description: 食事どきには、列ができることで有名な「テジ(豚)クッパ」の店で、釜山の多くのテジクッパ専門店の中でも特に有名だ。肉が柔らかく美味。

records.name: ベジナラン (베지나랑)
records.address: 水営区 広安海辺路 370番キル 9-32ノーブルスカイ9階
records.menu: 黒米豆カツ, アボカドロール
records.description:
毎日仕入れる新鮮な野菜で味をつけ、手軽なサラダから一品料理、 
コース料理まで豊富なメニューが楽しめるビーガンレストラン。
ビーガンレストランらしく外国人客が多く訪れるという。

records.name: ソクファ韓定食 (석화한정식)
records.menu: ソクファ韓定食, ソクファコヒャン韓定食
records.description: 料理１品１品が食べるのがもったいないほど繊細に盛りつけられて出てくる。 格式ある集まりの場所としても有名な高級韓定食専門店で、ポソッタンス(きのこの甘酢揚げ)やジョンボクチョ(アワビの煮つけ)が出てくるコヒャン韓定食と、貝柱の刺身やカルビチム、焼きウナギが出てくるオモニ韓定食が代表メニュー。

records.name: ネダン (내당)
records.address: 東莱区 金剛公園路 20番キル 23 ホテル農心 別館
records.menu: 一品一膳(平日ランチ特選)１人, ヨンコース(コースメニュー)１人
records.description:
庭園と池がある伝統家屋形式の古風な趣を備え
たお店で、伝統的な韓国料理を多彩に楽しむこ
とができる。各種宴会にふさわしい上品なお店。

records.name: ボンレストラン (봉식당)
records.address: 釜山広域市東莱区温泉路119番ギル26
records.description:
韓国料理店を経営していた母とフレンチシェフ
の息子が営むお店で、旬の素材を生かしたコー
スや仕上げのポッサムが特徴的。 各種イベント
会場としても多く利用される。

records.name: 60年の伝統 ハルメクッパ (60년 전통 할매국밥)
records.address: 東区 中央大路533番ギル4
records.menu:
タロクッパ ￦7,000
ゆで肉白飯 ￦9,000
records.description:
60年の伝統を持つ、テジクッパ専門店で、食事時間には、30分以上並ばないといけないという程、有名
な店だ。一般的なテジクッパとは違い、澄んだスープが特徴。大まかにスライスされたゆで豚肉は、予
想以上にまろやかな味。
スープと肉を混ぜない状態で出されるゆで肉白飯「スユクペッパン」が特に人気。

records.name: 咸鏡麺屋 (함경면옥)
records.menu: 冷麺, 王カルビタン, 王餃子 小
records.description: 30年の実力を持つ職人が作った冷麺の味は比べ物にならない。 釜山で最も有名な冷麺専門店のひとつで、季節を問わず訪れる多くのお客さんがこの店の変わらぬ味を証明している。

records.name: ワッダシクタン (왔다식당)
records.menu: スジゆで肉, スジ入りテンジャンの寄せ鍋
records.description:
日本人客もよく訪れるこの店は、約30年間営む韓牛スジ料理専門店で、 
柔らかい食感のスジは必ず韓牛だけを使うという。
代表メニューであるテンジャンの寄せ鍋を食べる時は、必ずラーメンを追加してみて。

records.name: 亀浦村素麺
records.address: 金井区 クムセム路490
records.description:
メニューは素麺(グクス)一品のみ。 南海岸の最
高級カタクチイワシ4~5種を混ぜて12時間以上
煮込んだスープを使うこのお店は、2代にわたり
30年以上営業している有名な素麺専門店。誰に
でも自信を持ってお勧めできるお店

records.name: オルクニソンカルグッス (얼크니손칼국수 )
records.address: 釜山広域市機張郡機張邑車城路417番ギル22
records.menu: オルクニソンカルグクス, 餃子
records.description: 簡単にしゃぶしゃぶをいただいた後に、麺を入れていただくカルグクス。材料たっぷり でボリュームがあるのにお値段はリーズナブル。最初はしゃぶしゃぶ、そのスープにカ ルグクスを入れて、残ったスープにご飯を入れ、店員がチャーハンを作ってくれる。

records.name: タムボク (탐복 본점)
records.address: 機張郡 日光邑 文五城キル 31
records.menu:
タムボク粥、タムボク飯 ￦18,000
タムボク焼き ￦39,000
records.description: 素敵な盛り付けの国内産アワビ料理、シグネチャーのアワビの内臓ソースなどアワビ料理を専門とするカジュアルな韓国料理を提供するお店。古い家屋を活用した韓国式+カジュアルインテリアが素敵。

records.name: コングク (곤국)
records.address: 釜山広域市南区荒嶺通り74番ギル51-1
records.menu: 韓牛コムタン, 韓牛筋ゆで肉
records.description: 牛肉や骨をじっくり煮込んだスープ「コムタン」の専門店。よく煮込まれた柔らかい 肉と、濃厚なスープが特徴的。ご飯を入れずに炊きたての釜飯が別に提供される。

records.name: ヘナム食堂 (해남식당)
records.address: 釜山広域市南区盆浦路145（龍湖洞Ｗスクェア）  龍湖洞Ｗスクェア
records.menu: 古漬けゆで肉焼き, 昔風キムチチゲ
records.description: キムチ料理専門の店で、白菜産地として有名な海南の白菜を使って、長い時間熟 成させた古漬けにこだわるのが特徴で、様々なキムチ料理を味わうことができる。 海南古漬けの高い誇りを持っている。

records.name: 凡一ピンデトッ (범일빈대떡)
records.menu:
ピンデトッ ￦10,000
パジョン(ネギチヂミ) ￦12,000
records.description:
「ぺク・ジョンウォンの三大天王」という有名な料理バラエティー番組で紹介されたことがある、
今では珍しい緑豆チヂミ「ピンデトッ」専門店。
昔ながらの感性を持っているこの店の代表メニュー「ピンデトッ」の生地は100％緑豆を使い、
小麦粉よりも香ばしく、伝統酒にもよく合う。

records.name: 金剛餃子 (금강만두)
records.address: 東莱区社稷北路5番ギル11
records.menu: 忠武(チュンム)セット(忠武のり巻き+餃子スープ), ユッケジャン
records.description:
美食家だけが訪れる隠れた名店として知られていたが
現在は多くの人々が気軽に訪れることができるよう広い店舗に移り営業している。 
餃子だけでなく、さっぱりした味のユッケジャンが有名なお店。

records.name: ソッカジョン (석화정)
records.menu: 牡蛎クッパ, 生牡蛎
records.description:
20年以上営んでいるカキ料理専門店で、旬の生牡蛎、牡蛎焼き、牡蛎フライ、牡蛎チヂミ、牡蛎キムチな
ど、牡蛎を使ったいろいろな料理を楽しむことができる。特に代表メニューである牡蛎「クル」クッパは、
新鮮な天然の牡蛎を使い、旨みがしっかり出たスープが人気。

records.name: 蓮山ナクチヘムルタン (연산낙지해물탕)
records.address: 釜山広域市蓮堤区瓜亭路121
records.menu: ヘムルタン、サンナクチ鍋
records.description: 海鮮鍋すなわち「ヘムルタン」は、元々ボリュームたっぷりのシーフード料理だ が、この店の海鮮鍋は誰もが新鮮だとわかるような魚介類が、蓋が閉まらない ほどたくさん入っている。火が通ったのを見計らって、活きたタコ「ナクチ」を入 れてくれる。

records.name: オッパダアワビ蔘鶏湯 (옻바다 전복삼계탕)
records.address: 釜山広域市蓮堤区ワールドカップ通り119番ギル16
records.menu: 漆サムゲタン、サムゲタン
records.description: 蓮山洞中心部の路地にある参鶏湯専門店で、代表的なスタミナ食である漆サムゲタン (蔘鶏湯)にアワビも追加できるのが特徴。食前酒として漆酒が提供される。テレビ番組 でも紹介された有名なレストラン。

records.name: タリジプ (다리집)
records.address: 水営区 南川パダ路 10番キル 70 101号
records.menu: トッポッキ, Aセット
records.description:
釜山で有名なトッポッキ専門店の一つで、屋台で商売をしていた頃に 
お客さんの足(タリ)だけが外から見えることから、タリチブと呼ばれるようになったこのお店は
一本だけ食べてもお腹がいっぱいになりそうな大きめのトッポッキとイカの天ぷらが有名。

records.name: 広安里オンヤンプルコギ 釜山店(광안리 언양불고기부산집)
records.address: 釜山広域市水営区南川パダ路32
records.description:
30年以上の伝統がある広安里オンヤンプルコ
ギ店で、厳選された100%韓牛雌牛と自ら栽培
した有機農作物を使用する。説明を必要としな
い有名店の一つ。

records.name: 食堂3選徳川店 (식당 3선)
records.address: 釜山広域市北区金谷通り112
records.menu: 味付け豚カルビ、コチュジャン豚カルビ
records.description: 炭火焼き、ネギサムギョプ焼き、小麦麺などを味わうことができる。老若男女・年齢に関 わらず楽しむことができる大衆的な味わいが特徴。広々としいるので、家族連れでの外 食にも人気がある。メイン料理の炭火焼きは、調理された状態で提供され、食べやすい。

records.name: 咸鏡麺屋 (함경면옥)
records.address: 釜山広域市北区金谷通り21
records.description: 22年の伝統がある咸興冷麺専門店で、メニューに使われる食材は全て手作り。サツ マイモの澱粉特有の弾力とコシがある咸興冷麺が特徴であり、濃厚なスープがおい しい水冷麺と、熟成されたエイの刺身が特に美味しい刺身ビビン麺が人気メニュー。

records.name: モンシル宗家テジクッパ  (몽실종가돼지국밥)
records.address: 西区 カチゴゲ路197番ギル3, 1階
records.description:
甘川文化村の近くにあるテジクッパ専門店で、清潔な室内と親切な店員が印象的だ。牛の骨を24時間
以上じっくり煮込んだスープが有名で、クッパに入れる肉の量と種類を選択できるのが特徴だ。

records.name: トンウォン長寿村
records.menu: 緑豆韓方水炊き, ヌンイ水炊き
records.description:
陶芸家が焼いた素敵な丸い器に料理を盛り付ける補養食専門店。宴会などの各種集まりにも人気が
ある。韓方緑豆水炊き「ハンバンノクトゥペクス」が特に人気で、キバナオウギやクコ、甘草などの韓薬
剤で、緑豆アヒルを長時間煮込んだ補薬(漢方薬)のようなスープと柔らかい肉が絶品。

records.name: 浦項カジャミムルフェ (포항가자미물회)
records.menu: 夏の刺身の冷たいスープ, 冬の刺身の冷たいスープ
records.description: 素朴な雰囲気のお店で、冷たいムルフェ(刺身のスープ)に麺を入れて食べることで有名なムルフェ専門店。 あらゆる調味料で和えた刺身と刺身の出汁が別々に提供され、夏には新鮮なトマトに包んで食べ、冬にはのりで包んで食べるのが特徴的だ。

records.name: 掛法チュックミ (괘법쭈꾸미)
records.menu: ウェルビンチュックミ
records.description: 2007年に掛法洞で営業し始めたこの地域の代表的なチュックミ(イイダコ)料理専門店。手作りのビビンソースを使って、辛いがなぜか食べてしまう味が特徴的だ。 代表メニューはウェルビンチュックミで、このメニュー１つをずっと変わらず守ってきたことが長年の人気の秘訣。

records.name: 鳴旨チョッチブ(명지첫집)
records.address: 江西区鳴旨国際6路232番ギル18
records.menu: イイダコのポサム(M), ポサム定食 ランチ特選 2人前
records.description:
ボリュームがうれしいポサム定食やイイダコのポサムが代表メニューで
鳴旨(ミョンジ)を象徴する食材である塩と長ネギを使った塩辛や長ネギキムチをポサム料理に添
えて提供してくれる。

records.name: 名品外食ユンミョンジョン (명품외식 육면정)
records.menu: 骨なし生カルビ, 味付けカルビ, 骨なし味付けカルビ焼き
records.description:
宴会場や子供向けのルーム、広い駐車場を備えた大規模な焼き肉専門店で、質
の高い牛肉と新鮮な野菜を提供し衛生面においても最高レベルと承認された。 
団体の集まりや家族での外食に最適と言える。

records.name: ピョンサノク (평산옥)
records.menu: ゆで肉, 素麺, 大根の若菜入りキムチ素麺
records.description:
4代にわたって続いてきた100年の伝統を持つ老舗テジスユクという豚
のゆで肉専門食堂。テジスユクとスープに入れて食べる「ククス」（麺）が
有名だ。国産の新鮮な肉で作るスープは澄んでいて、さっぱりした深みの
ある味わい。100年間続く店としての誇りにふさわしい味だ。

records.name: コンガム食堂 (공감식당)
records.menu: 選別熟成サムギョプサル, 選別熟成モクサル（肩ロース）
records.description:
大麦を飼料として与えた豚を専門家が選別している。肉は熟成させた後、専門教
育を受けた従業員が丁寧に焼いてくれる焼き肉専門店。サムギョプサルと一緒に
焼くチーズがこの店の人気メニュー。サイドメニューも豊富に用意されている。

records.name: タオム（西面サムジョンタワー店） (다옴)
records.address: 釜山市釜山鎮区中央大路672、サムジョンタワー5階
records.menu: 牛のともばら肉のビビン素麺, カルグクス, 素麺, ビビンバ
records.hours:
月曜日～木曜日、日曜日：11:00-22:00
(21:00ラストオーダー)
金曜日～土曜日：11:00-22:30(ラストオーダー20:30頃)
(21:30ラストオーダー)
records.description:
気軽に楽しめる韓国料理を提供するお店で、南海岸のカタクチイワシの出汁や果
物を煮込んだ熟成タレなど真心を込めて準備する。「チャドルバギ」（牛のともばら
肉）がトッピングされた「ビビングクス」（ビビン素麺）とビビンバが代表メニュー。

records.name: タンガムミルミョン (당감밀면)
records.address: 釜山市釜山鎮区堂甘路5、 サムイクアパートサンガ B棟 1階
records.menu: ミルミョン, ビビンミルミョン, 手作り餃子4個, 8個, 手打ち麺
records.description:
地域住民が推薦する「ミルミョン」すなわち小麦粉の冷麺専門店。スープはも
ちろん、麺やヤンニョムに至るまですべてシェフ独自の秘法で作っており、独
特な味を誇る。手作り餃子も淡泊な味で人気がある。

records.name: ヤンピョンカルグクス (양평칼국수)
records.menu: ヤンピョンカルグクス, ビビンカルグクス, ミョルチカルグクス, 肉餃子
records.description: 多大浦海水浴場の近くにあるお店で、職人歴20年のカルグクス職人が作った熟成麺に韓国産の白菜で毎日漬けるキムチが本当に美味しい。夏にしか味わえない冷カルグクス、豆乳冷きしめんなどの限定メニューも人気だ。

records.name: ヨンジンテジクッパ 本店 (영진돼지국밥본점)
records.address: 釜山沙下区下新繁栄路157番キル39
records.description: 有名な豚クッパ専門店の一つで、いつも人々で賑わっている。豚特有の臭みを取り除き、淡泊な味が自慢だ。ゆで肉や豆腐、キムチ炒めがセットになった「スユクペッパン」といわれるゆで肉定食が人気。

records.name: トンウォン　スップルカルビ (동원 숯불 갈비)
records.address: 釜山蓮堤区瓜亭路276番キル9
records.hours:
10:00-22:00
(21:00ラストオーダー)

*月曜日は隔週で営業
records.description: 静かな路地にたたずむ豚カルビ専門店は、38年間、炭火豚カルビのメニューひとつでお店を守ってきた。見つけにくい場所にあるが、親しみやすくいつも変わらない味で多くの常連客が訪れる。

records.name: ドナルド即席トッポッキ (도날드)
records.address: 影島区ツクムナムギル267
records.description: 地域住民にとって思い出の場所であるこのお店は、35年間続く有名な即席トッポッキ専門店で、海鮮出汁と唐辛子味噌のソースで作った独特な味が自慢。トッポッキを食べた後はスイーツ「ポンクリーム」まであり、これを食べるために訪れる人も多い。

records.name: 咸興ポッサム (함흥보쌈)
records.menu: 盛り合わせポッサム, 咸興冷麺, 平壌冷麺
records.description: 冷麺専門店からスタートした約50年間続くポッサム専門店で、新鮮な肉を使用し、柔らかく口当たりがいいことで有名。長い伝統を誇る冷麺も人気で、どのメニューもボリュームがあり大満足間違いなし。

records.name: 元山麺屋
records.menu: 平壌冷麺, 咸興冷麺
records.description: 60年以上の伝統がある冷麺専門店で、3代目が経営する有名なお店。韓牛と韓国産の豚肉、鶏肉を使用し10種類以上の材料が入ったスープで作った冷麺はいつも変わらない味が自慢だ。

records.name: ケミジプ新都市店（ナクチ炒めケミジプ）
records.address: 釜山海雲台区佐洞路10番キル 51-5
records.menu: ナクチ炒め, ホルモン鍋
records.description: 釜山の代表的なタコ「ナクチ」料理専門店「ケミジプ」のチェーン店で、本店にも遜色ない美味しさ。本店と同じようにナクチやナクチ・エビ、ナクチ・ホルモン炒めなどが人気料理。焼肉ナクチキノコ鍋とホルモン鍋を注文する利用客も多い。

records.name: オリハンサン (오리한상)
records.address: 鳴旨国際9路66ジボンビル2階
records.menu: 鴨の塩焼き, 鴨の味付け焼き
records.description: マガモの塩焼きと急速冷凍した鴨肉を薄くスライスしたプルゴギが人気のこのお店は、大きな窓を活かした清潔で余裕のある店内や個室があり、家族連れの外食にも最適。

records.name: マンポミルミョン (만포밀면)
records.address: 機張邑チャソン路322番ギル40
records.menu: ムルミルミョン, ビビンミルミョン, 蒸し餃子
records.description: お店に足を踏み入れると濃厚なスープの香りが漂う当店は、伽耶風の小麦麺を作っている。95年に開店して以来、毎日その日に販売する小麦麺を味見することから始まるという。 いつも変わらない味が嬉しい。

records.name: マッサランチェ (맛사랑채)
records.menu: 野菜包み定食, さばの煮付け, 鶏肉の炒め煮
records.description: 焼き魚を含む12種類のおかずとともに日替わりのスープが提供される定食は、家のご飯よりもさらに家庭の味だと評価されている。 人情あふれる食膳を味わうため遠方から訪れるお客さんも多い。

records.name: ウジョンカマンチョンテジ (우정까망촌돼지)
records.description: 焼きもの専門店のこの店は、子供の頃田舎で食べたことのある豚肉の味を再現するために清浄地域で育てられた豚を空輸している。 釜の蓋で焼いて食べるのが特徴的で味もおいしいが、焼けるまで待つのがつらいほどだ。

records.name: ペッコプシゲ (배꼽시계)
records.address: 日光面ジャンゴクギル63-14
records.menu: 黄漆硫黄入り鴨肉の水炊き, ヌンイ硫黄入り鴨肉の水炊き, 鴨のプルコギ
records.description: 薬膳料理を一筋に、手術を終えた患者さんもよく訪れるほど健康に良い料理を作る鴨料理専門店。季節の食材を使って漬物を漬け、2年以上熟成させたキムチを使用する。 鴨の水炊きは時間がかかるため、2時間以上前に予約しよう。

records.name: サランド フェッチブ (사랑도 횟집)
records.menu: 天然産の刺身, ウニのビビンバ, ムルフェ(冷たい刺身のスープ)
records.description: 毎日新鮮なお刺身を仕込み、自家製のおかずで食卓を満たす。 料理に正直に営むこのお店は、常連客が多いことで有名な刺身屋だ。少々値段が高めだと思われがちだが、料理が並べられた後にはむしろ安く感じるだろう。

records.name: 釜山豚足 (부산족발)
records.menu: チョッパル(豚足),ネンチェチョッパル(冷菜豚足)
records.description: 富平洞の豚足通りに位置する豚足専門店で、テレビ番組でもよく紹介される有名なお店。この地域は、釜山の郷土料理である冷菜豚足が誕生した場所として有名である。このお店でも淡白で弾力のある豚足と冷菜豚足が味わえる。

records.name: 南浦参鶏湯 (남포삼계탕)
records.description: 光復路ファッション通りの近くにあるこのお店は、50年以上営業してきた参鶏湯専門店。代表メニューの参鶏湯は、お腹の中にもち米、高麗人参、栗、ナツメを詰めた鶏一羽をスープに入れ、土鍋で沸かしたまま出てくる。 電気オーブン焼きも人気。

records.name: デスジョン (대수정)
records.menu: 釜飯定食, カルビチム定食, 韓牛タダク定食
records.description: 40年以上営業してきた韓国料理専門店。直接運営する農場から仕入れた材料で味噌や醤油、キムチなどを作っており、上質の韓牛を使用する。 釜飯と一緒に並べられるテーブルいっぱいのおかずが嬉しい。

records.name: ドンチョンファンジョン スンスユクジョンゴル (동촌황정순수육전골)
records.menu: スユクジョンゴル(ゆで肉の寄せ鍋), しゃぶしゃぶ
records.description: 刺激的ではないが濃厚な味のスープが特徴的で、あらかじめ茹でて油を取り除いた肉を厚く切って使うので食感がよい。 すべての材料は国内産を使用し、２つのメニューのみを真心を込めて提供する。

records.name: ソウダッケ (소우닭계)
records.menu: 辛味カルビチム定食, 王カルビタン, 韓牛ユッケジャン
records.description: 店名のように牛(ソ)と鶏(ダッ)を使った韓国料理を専門に扱うお店で、オーナーシェフの秘法で作った柔らかいカルビチムが有名。 おかずも直接準備しており、１人でもカルビチムを食べられるメニューが嬉しい。

records.name: ヤンジ チュオタン (양지추어탕)
records.menu: チュオタン(ドジョウのスープ), ドジョウの天ぷら, コダリチム(スケトウダラの蒸し物)
records.description: 大きな釜で煮込んだチュオタン(ドジョウのスープ)に農家から仕入れた粉唐辛子を入れ、自家製のキムチを使用する安心できるお店。 手頃な価格でおいしくボリュームたっぷりの料理が提供されるため常連客が多いという。

records.name: 草梁トンダック (초량통닭)
records.menu: メニュー フライド, 鶏肉の炒め煮, 水炊き
records.description: 1976年から40年以上営業してきたこのお店は、この地域では知らない人がほとんどいないほど有名。 肉汁あふれるフライドチキンは長年愛されてきたメニューで、いつも会社帰りの会社員でいっぱい。

records.name: モグムジク (먹음직)
records.description: 温泉川カフェ通りにある焼き物専門店。流通業も共に営んでおり、いつも新鮮な肉を用意している。 直接熟成させた肉はもちろん、すべての料理を誠実に丁寧に提供するお店として高い評価を受けている。

records.name: セヨンジョン (세연정)
records.menu: 特カルビ, 味付けカルビ2本, カルビの塩焼き
